thesis_or_destination: "This project is a faithful re-implementation of Chris Nesbitt-Smith's (CNS) Policy as [Versioned] Code thesis onto Flux CD. Source material: the talk, the original Medium post, the later 'mea culpa' blog post, and two reference GitHub orgs (example-policy-org, policy-as-versioned-code)." Also: "Fidelity = 'faithful to intent.' Reproduce the thesis and its ethos 1:1, but let Flux do natively what the 2022 implementation had to hack ... The PRD targets this faithful-to-intent floor; a separate modern-reference report documents the fuller 'north star' design." (CONTEXT.md)

decisions.title: Transport: signed git tags, keyless (gitsign)
decisions.status: referenced only (not read from ADR file; described in CONTEXT.md prose)
decisions.gist: Policy distributed as semver git tags, signed keyless with sigstore/gitsign, consumed via a Flux GitRepository pinned on spec.ref.tag AND spec.ref.commit. Known limitation accepted: no Flux-native verified-source admission gate on the floor (Flux verify is PGP-only), pending upstream fluxcd/source-controller#1068.

decisions.title: Adoption cadence: pinned everywhere + Renovate PR
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: Consumers and clusters pin exact tags; new versions land only via a reviewed Renovate PR (automerge:false). Live semver ranges rejected. Adoption cadence and enforcement action are independent axes.

decisions.title: Engine: Kyverno; policies authored as CEL ValidatingPolicy
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: Kyverno ValidatingPolicy with validationActions: Audit = lane-keeping; Deny = gate.

decisions.title: Cloud plane: fork/harvest collie
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: Cloud plane built by harvesting ControlPlane's collie (OSCAL catalogue + policy intent as data); its generator/Lula toolchain and bootstrap dropped.

decisions.title: Install/fleet layer: ControlPlane Flux Operator
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: FluxInstance + ResourceSet matrix used as install + fleet layer; thesis stays vanilla-Flux-expressible.

decisions.title: Deterministic policy — no time conditions
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: Policy bodies contain no time-conditional logic; same manifest + same policy version always evaluates the same.

decisions.title: Agent-assisted editorial governance
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: Human-governance layer realised as editorial review (reviewed PR), supported by the agent governance layer.

decisions.title: OSCAL attestation via C2P
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: C2P's result2oscal consumes Kyverno PolicyReports to produce OSCAL assessment-results — carrier of the 'measurable' pillar's control attestation.

decisions.title: Sunset: scheduled proposals, not scheduled application
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: A fleet's array entry may carry a sunset date; on that date a machine opens a retirement PR a human must merge — nothing timed ever changes an admission verdict on its own.

decisions.title: Composed artefact: self-signed, pinned SHA
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: Adopter signs its composed artefact as any publisher signs an artefact, carrying each parent's resolved commit SHA; a verifier re-renders and checks byte-for-byte.

decisions.title: Regulator publishes baselines, adopter selects
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: Regulator publishes named, signed OSCAL baselines; adopter selects one and may add controls but never remove one. Control id identity is the bare catalogue id, exact-string resolution.

decisions.title: Unclaimed is caged; governed namespace requires claim
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: Orphan guard denies admission of a workload claiming a retired version; a pod with no claim is out of scope unless in a governed namespace, where unclaimed is denied on CREATE only (UPDATE excluded for de-posturing).

decisions.title: Adopter runs the proposer and it opens the PR
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: Proposer runs in the adopter's repo against its own composed artefact; bounded by confidence floor, rate limit, rejection ledger; no merge()/approve(); starts on merged version-pin bump or human dispatch, never a clock.

decisions.title: A subclass never restates a Mutate
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: Restatement applies only to ValidatingPolicy on the Audit<Deny ladder; a composition restating a MutatingPolicy/GeneratingPolicy is refused.

decisions.title: A control claim belongs to whoever ships the implementation
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: A control claim is a signed statement in a party's OSCAL component-definition that a policy it ships evidences a control id; a party may never claim against another party's policy.

decisions.title: The namespace manifest is the governed declaration
decisions.status: referenced only
decisions.gist: The governed label on the adopter's Namespace manifest is the declaration, signed under the same tag as the composed artefact; only the adopter adds a governed namespace, by hand — the proposer never proposes one.

rejections_and_supersessions: "Exemption — A banned concept. There are none, ever. ... The estate shipped an exemptions ledger that contradicted this; it is removed — see `.scratch/govern-what-you-dont-control/issues/05-remove-the-exemption-ledger.md`." (CONTEXT.md)

"Reproduce the thesis and its ethos 1:1, but let Flux do natively what the 2022 implementation had to hack (the scaffolding that only existed because GitOps tooling couldn't yet express 'versioned policy as a live dependency' is dropped, not preserved)." (CONTEXT.md)
"No bespoke tooling. ... no wrapper, no re-implemented `policy-checker`. The 2022 bash/Docker checker is deleted, not ported." (CONTEXT.md)
"We harvest its reusable IP ... and rebuild the cloud plane natively; its generator/Lula/bootstrap are dropped (ADR-0004)." (CONTEXT.md, re: collie)
"a weakening is never an override and never an exemption, it is a declared inability that is caged and priced" (CONTEXT.md, on Restatement)
"a removal is an exemption by another name, and a control the adopter cannot meet is caged and priced, not dropped" (CONTEXT.md, on Baseline)
open_items: "The last-mile problem ... An explicitly acknowledged open problem, not something the system claims to solve." (CONTEXT.md)

"Known limitation (accepted): Flux GitRepository.spec.verify is PGP-only and cannot verify gitsign signatures today, so there is no Flux-native verified-source admission gate on the floor. ... pending upstream fluxcd/source-controller#1068 (a tracked project action — see docs/upstream/)." (CONTEXT.md)
"Deferred to north-star (need OCI): signed attestations carrying the 'why', and SBOM." (CONTEXT.md)
"Compliance / measurable ... In the original this was a proxy ('a GitHub PR search away'). See open question on proxy-vs-ground-truth." (CONTEXT.md) — referenced but not resolved in this file
"A real-cloud e2e (live RDS/S3, optional LocalStack provisioning, C2P over realized state) is optional and documented." (CONTEXT.md)
notes: CONTEXT.md self-describes as "a glossary, not a spec — no implementation details," so it has no build tickets and no direct implementation claims; all ADR content here is CONTEXT.md's own paraphrase of decisions, since the ADR files themselves were outside the paths given for this group. docs/agents/domain.md and docs/agents/issue-tracker.md are process/meta docs (how to consume domain docs, where issues live) with no decisions or claims of their own. CLAUDE.md is a two-line pointer to those same docs/agents/*.md files. No status lines or dates exist anywhere in these four files (prose-glossary format, not ticket format) — the "status" field on each decision is filled with "referenced only" rather than a verbatim status line, since none exists. The exemption-ledger removal is the only concrete cross-reference to another effort's artifact (.scratch/govern-what-you-dont-control/issues/05-remove-the-exemption-ledger.md) — worth checking against that group's own inventory.

thesis_or_destination: "policy — the rules that mitigate risk — should be treated like any other software dependency: versioned, distributed, tested, updated by reviewed pull request" ... "most of an enterprise's real policy surface is *lane-keeping*, continuous corrective guidance, and a system that only knows how to say \"no\" repeats the original mistake. This repo re-implements that corrected thesis faithfully, on Flux CD, as a real, runnable, live-verified system — not a slide deck." (docs/HISTORY.md). SHOW-AND-TELL.md restates it as: "treat a body of governance policy like a software dependency — semantically versioned, signed, pinned, distributed, unit-tested, and updated by reviewed PR — *not* primarily a deploy-time gate," scored against seven "-ables": visible, communicable, consumable, testable, usable, updatable, measurable.

decisions.title: Two-org split (components org vs consuming model org)
decisions.status: Deferred — explicitly named during grilling, deliberately not acted on
decisions.gist: Componentization (pr-gate-action, c2p-collector, handbook-generator, readiness-collector as own repos) is real, but all still live in one policy-as-versioned-flux org. Splitting into a components org vs a model-consuming org is called out as a real, separate decision, not scope creep to fold into this epic.

decisions.title: Fresh-org redeploy ("clean history")
decisions.status: Deferred — named as the project's eventual sequel
decisions.gist: A viewer asked for clean history during the demo; the answer is not rewriting this org's history but a future from-scratch redeploy into a fresh org, proving reproducibility, while this org stays as the record of how it was actually built, thrashing included. "No history rewrite happens in place, ever."

decisions.title: History rewrite / repo recreation with clean history
decisions.status: RECOMMEND AGAINST (pre-grilling verdict; alternative offered)
decisions.gist: Rejects squashing/recreating fleet (and hard-nos policy) history: contradicts the project's append-only audit-trail ethos, breaks GitHub-API-sourced dashboard history, and the underlying newcomer-presentable need is better served by docs/HISTORY.md. If wanted after grilling: fleet-only, never policy, own dedicated confirmation.

decisions.title: Extract pr-gate-check.sh into a separate reusable Action/repo
decisions.status: DEFER (YAGNI today)
decisions.gist: Exactly one real consumer (fleet) exists today; extracting now creates a governed dependency with no second consumer to justify it. Revisit when a second config repo appears.

decisions.title: Policy versions should have a sunset time
decisions.status: RECONCILABLE with ADR-0006 via reframe — needs a new ADR (later realized as ADR-0010)
decisions.gist: ADR-0006 rejects timed enforcement changes; fix is a sunset field on the fleet array entry (adoption-scoped, not part of the immutable policy release), dashboard time-to-sunset, governance-agent escalation, and at the date a machine opens a retirement PR a human must merge — nothing timed ever applies automatically. Needs a short ADR because it deliberately extends ADR-0006's boundary.

decisions.title: ADR-0010: sunset scheduled proposals, not application
decisions.status: Adopted (cited, not reproduced in this group)
decisions.gist: Sunset is framed as a scheduled proposal (a machine-opened PR a human must merge) never a scheduled application — extends ADR-0006's determinism boundary deliberately, leaning on ADR-0002's 'machine-opened, human-merged' precedent.

tickets.title: cluster-state Flux Kustomization for policy-versions.yaml / apps.yaml
tickets.status: Fixed for real, not patched around
tickets.acceptance_gist: policy-versions.yaml and apps.yaml get the same self-healing git-drives-cluster guarantee every other resource already had, instead of being one-shot kubectl apply'd by up.sh and never touched again.
tickets.evidence_claimed: fleet#55 (new Kustomization); re-proven live with two follow-up PRs fleet#56/#57 — install a throwaway version and watch Flux install it with zero manual steps, remove it and watch Flux prune it automatically.
tickets.honesty_flags: Found by an adversarial audit after the epic was marked done: the ResourceSet had quietly drifted out of band (hand-edited version field), was actively denying two running apps at admission when found; ticket 09's original claim had never been tested against a continuously-reconciling cluster.

tickets.evidence_claimed: fleet#19 PR; SHOW-AND-TELL.md demo reproduces a spoofed-bump failure via pr-gate-check.sh (declares 2.2.1, tag still renders 2.2.0 -> FAIL exit 1).
tickets.honesty_flags: Originally a CONFIRMED GAP in raw feedback (NOTES.md item 5): gate never cross-checked declared version against rendered content.

tickets.evidence_claimed: fleet#49
tickets.honesty_flags: Found by the adversarial audit as one of four smaller-but-real gaps behind 'done' status.

tickets.title: Weekly governance nag 'skips already-actioned issues' checkbox
tickets.status: Now genuinely implemented and proven live
tickets.acceptance_gist: The checkbox claiming the nag skips already-actioned issues had no code behind it; now implemented, including proof of the case where it correctly does NOT skip.
tickets.evidence_claimed: fleet#50

tickets.title: Forge-level tag-immutability protection across tagged repos
tickets.status: Fixed to match the one repo (policy) that already had it right
tickets.acceptance_gist: Eight of nine tagged repos had no forge-level tag-immutability protection at all, contradicting ADR-0001's own stated requirement.
tickets.evidence_claimed: Narrated fix in HISTORY.md (no PR number given)

tickets.title: Daily cron workflow running sunset-escalator.sh
tickets.status: Fixed with a real daily-cron GitHub Actions workflow
tickets.acceptance_gist: sunset-escalator.sh's logic was real and demonstrated by hand, but nothing in the estate ever invoked it — ADR-0010's 'machine opens a retirement PR on the date' was aspirational, not automated.
tickets.evidence_claimed: fleet#58, runs against fleet using the workflow's own same-repo GITHUB_TOKEN, no new cross-repo secret; SHOW-AND-TELL.md: 'A daily GitHub Actions workflow runs the escalator unattended (three real runs on the record)'; gh issue 30 cited as a live escalation issue.
tickets.honesty_flags: Known caveat stated plainly in SHOW-AND-TELL.md: the retirement-PR path is fixed end-to-end except for one org setting — 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests' — OFF org-wide, needs an admin toggle. Script still never calls gh pr merge.

tickets.acceptance_gist: cp-10_smt finding used to mis-attribute to an unrelated fixture; now correctly attributes to datastore's own non-compliant RDS claim.

tickets.title: Orphan guard extended to cover Crossplane CRs
tickets.acceptance_gist: The cloud plane's orphan guard now also covers Crossplane custom resources, matching the workload-plane guard.

notes: docs/HISTORY.md is unusually self-referential: it documents at least four in-place self-corrections to its own earlier drafts (the 'day-old not year-old' claim, the over-corrected 'entire project spans 2026-07-14 to 2026-07-18' claim, ticket 09's 'never actually merged' broad claim, ticket 16's wrong ADR-0005 citation). docs/SHOW-AND-TELL.md's footer states audits ran '5 waves this session,' while docs/HISTORY.md's own narrative names only two explicit passes ('a second wave' and 'a later pass') plus the original build — the exact count of 5 vs the passes actually narrated in HISTORY.md is not reconciled in this group's sources. .scratch/demo-feedback/CONCLUSIONS.md is explicitly pre-grilling and provisional; several of its research-pending items (readiness-collector's kyverno CLI support, item 13's onboarding-PR questions) are not explicitly closed out anywhere in this same group's sources, even though docs/HISTORY.md describes the readiness-collector and Renovate as built/live — treat CONCLUSIONS.md as superseded-in-substance but not formally closed within these four files. NOTES.md item 12 itself flags an internal tension with ADR-0006 that CONCLUSIONS.md resolves via a reframe and HISTORY.md later cites as resolved by ADR-0010 — the resolution chain runs across all three files. The ledger CVE-count reversal directly contradicts ticket 12's original headline claim from the real-estate epic (not in this file set, only referenced) — kept deliberately as an honest, inconvenient finding. docs/SHOW-AND-TELL.md is written as a live runbook presupposing the estate is already fully built, describing capability as fact in present tense throughout, whereas docs/HISTORY.md flags which of those capabilities were fixed only after adversarial audits found them missing or broken — a reviewer relying only on SHOW-AND-TELL.md would miss the honesty caveats HISTORY.md records for the same features (cluster-state wiring, OSCAL mis-attribution, orphan guard cloud coverage).

notes: This directory contains only build/implementation tickets (26 of them), not separate decision/ADR records — ADRs (ADR-0001..0009) and the PRD/CONTEXT.md are referenced throughout but live elsewhere in the repo, not under .scratch/faithful-floor/issues/. All 26 tickets show Status: done, but several carry substantial dated follow-up/correction sections added after initial completion (2026-07-17, 2026-07-18, 2026-07-20) from what tickets call 'wave-1' through 'wave-5' skeptic/audit passes — a recurring pattern across this epic of self-reported post-hoc corrections to earlier overclaims. Notable internal corrections/contradictions a reviewer should see: ticket 03 fixed a broken rationale cross-reference in main but deliberately did not re-tag/re-pin the 3 already-pinned versions (v1.0.3/v2.0.3/v2.2.0), calling it a considered, not accidental, gap. Ticket 07 corrected its own claim that CI caught two release incidents — only one actually was, the other found by manual review; also resolved its 'release notes' checklist item via GitHub Release edit rather than a new tag. Ticket 08 is the epic's central technical finding: Kyverno 1.18.2 flattens every installed ValidatingPolicy's objectSelector onto ONE shared ValidatingWebhookConfiguration (last-reconciled wins), silently breaking multi-version coexistence — fixed by switching to matchConditions CEL; ticket 08 also had a stale/superseded paragraph left standing until a wave-3 pass caught it, and a wave-2 audit found its dependsOn/wait verify check had been vacuously passing (wrong label selector, zero matches, loop body never ran) since creation. Ticket 09's 'changes in the same reconcile' claim was false for 3 days (policy-versions.yaml only kubectl-applied, not Flux-reconciled) until fleet#55; same root-cause gap recurred independently on cluster2 (ticket 10, fixed by fleet#62) and was traced by a wave-3 pass to a real, fully-deterministic kustomize-controller implicit-generation race, correcting an earlier 'flakiness' mischaracterization. Ticket 12 had a false 'reviewed, not self-merged' claim corrected by a wave-1 audit (GitHub's own record: zero reviews, self-merged, same as every PR in this solo-dev project). Ticket 19/09 found the orphan guard was structurally blind to unlabeled non-Pod resources (Crossplane CRs) until fleet#60 extended resourceRules. Ticket 20 found its own spike had leaked real writes onto the shared live cluster twice due to an unverified kubectl context assumption, fixed with a hard context guard. Ticket 23's 'never edits enforcement' guarantee was originally overclaimed as a scoped GitHub App token boundary; corrected to a code-level guarantee (no such scoped token was ever actually configured — all writes use full-access personal gh auth). Ticket 13's doc had a stale pinned-version table that silently diverged from reality for 3 days, then the fix itself introduced a v-prefix regression later caught by a wave-5 pass. Tickets 25/26 (handbook generator) were later extracted out of the policy repo into their own component repo by real-estate epic ticket 05, changing the invocation shape — noted in this epic's own corrections. Several tickets (11, 16, 17, 18, 20) record real live GitOps wiring as blocked behind a gitsign OAuth re-authentication step pending the user, later cleared 2026-07-15. Ticket 21 explicitly deviated from the ticket text's named 'github' Grafana datasource in favor of the unauthenticated 'infinity' datasource, disclosed in-panel. Ticket 24's noise-reduction/count claims are dated snapshots explicitly non-reproducible verbatim (the live advisory feed grows over time) — flagged in-ticket as expected variance, not error.

Ticket 04: v1.0.0 tag left in place broken (tag-flattening CI bug) because tag-protection ruleset blocks moving it and nothing depends on it; v1.0.1 is the first fully green release.

It also described app2/app3 (in the old apps monorepo) as "already working" in the present tense; that stopped being true 2026-07-16, when real-estate ticket 08 deleted app1/app2/app3 from the live cluster and archived the apps repo entirely ... superseding them with ledger/reports/api/datastore + storefront.' — policy-composition/faithful-floor 08
Ticket 13, describing docs/shift-left-dev-workflow.md: 'The 2022 bash/Docker checker stays deleted.' — 13

Ticket 19/25/26 headers: 'the pre-extraction location' language for fleet/pr-gate-check.sh and policy/handbook/generate.sh, both moved to standalone component repos by real-estate epic tickets 03 and 05.

Ticket 20: 'Confirmed cluster1's own ValidatingPolicy set was byte-for-byte unchanged before and after the run' after cleaning up leaked stray artifacts from an earlier contaminated run — rejecting the earlier state as invalid evidence.

Ticket 09 quoting ticket 03's Deny gate rationale: 'a candid note that this is the reference demonstrator for the Audit/Deny mechanism split ... not a claim that department labelling meets the gate's catastrophic-risk bar.' — 03

Ticket 08 major finding: Kyverno 'flattens EVERY installed ValidatingPolicy's objectSelector into ONE shared Kubernetes ValidatingWebhookConfiguration ... the last-reconciled policy silently wins' — rejects the design PRD §6.4 point 3 and CONTEXT.md's 'version self-scoping' specified as actually working; fixed by switching to matchConditions.
Ticket 10 checklist item: 'The silent-ungovernance gap of the 2022 implementation is demonstrably closed' — explicit supersession of the prior (2022) implementation's behavior.

Ticket 23, wave-1 correction: 'no such App or scoped token was ever actually set up ... The real guarantee was always the code-level one above, not a permission boundary; SPEC.md and governance-agent/README.md carried the same overclaim and are corrected alongside this.' — rejects an earlier overclaimed enforcement-boundary description.

Ticket 24, title/description correction: 'the delivered demonstrator deliberately opens a GitHub issue instead' of a PR as ADR-0007's Consequences section had committed to — 'the title/description never caught up to what was actually built and should have.'
Ticket 17: 'collie's generator/Lula/bootstrap stay dropped' — only the OSCAL catalogue/control-mapping intent is harvested, not collie's tooling.
Ticket 20: 'No second validation engine' (ADR-0009) paired with independent-schema-validation proof distinct from 'C2P twice'.
thesis_or_destination: No standalone thesis/mission statement file exists in this issues directory; the destination is expressed implicitly across all 26 tickets as building out the 'faithful-floor' epic: a versioned-policy-as-code control plane where policy is released as signed semver tags (ADR-0001), consumed via Flux GitOps ResourceSets across coexisting versions, enforced by Kyverno CEL ValidatingPolicies in Audit (lane-keeping) and Deny (gate) tiers, extended to a Crossplane cloud plane, made measurable via OSCAL/C2P and a CIO dashboard, updatable via a single Renovate surface, usable via native-CLI local reproduction, communicable via release notes/alerts, and governed by an advisory-metadata + editorial-review process with a bounded agent-governance layer that only ever proposes review, never edits enforcement. Ticket 10 states the throughline explicitly: 'the estate's gate strength equals its weakest installed version, so retiring is a security action' and that this closes 'the silent-ungovernance gap of the 2022 implementation.' Ticket 13 states the 2022 baseline being retired: 'The 2022 bash/Docker checker stays deleted.'

tickets.honesty_flags: Documents that determinism check is defence-in-depth only — Kyverno's CEL context structurally cannot read a policy's own metadata regardless, so the property already holds before any check runs. Correction: an earlier claim that a kustomize build check ran as part of the removal proof was false — it doesn't, only mentioned in a comment.

tickets.title: Agent governance layer: architectural spec
tickets.acceptance_gist: Spec covers signal ingestion, noise reduction, decision framing, PR/issue surfacing; never-edits-enforcement invariant stated with its enforcement mechanism; bounded demonstrator scope carved out.
tickets.evidence_claimed: New repo governance-agent, SPEC.md; three signal classes given differentiated treatment (CVE automatable, cloud/regulatory partial, Wardley climatic human-curated YAML); four-stage noise reduction; demonstrator scope committed to GitHub Security Advisories for kyverno/kyverno.
tickets.honesty_flags: Wave-1 correction: the claimed enforcement mechanism (a scoped GitHub App token with issues:write/contents:read, GitHub-API-enforced 403) was never actually set up — corrected to a code-level guarantee only (no git/gh pr call exists in the script), an overclaim present in SPEC.md and README.md too, corrected alongside. Wave-5 correction: 'only write is gh issue create' overlooked a gh label create call; corrected in 4 places; load-bearing claim (no enforcement-content writes) unaffected.

tickets.title: Agent demonstrator: one signal source -> review PR
tickets.acceptance_gist: Given a policy whose rationale is contradicted by a signal, agent opens a PR/issue framing the decision; proposes editorial review only, no enforcement file modified; noise reduction demonstrable (irrelevant signal -> no PR).
tickets.evidence_claimed: governance-agent/demonstrator.sh run live against real GitHub Security Advisories API for kyverno/kyverno: 27 fetched, 26 filtered as noise, 1 survivor (CVE-2026-54523) opened as 5 real GitHub issues (policy-as-versioned-flux/policy/issues/1-5); confirmed policy repo working tree/history untouched.
tickets.honesty_flags: Correction: title/description committed to 'opens a PR' but the delivered demonstrator opens a GitHub issue instead (checklist already hedged this correctly). Run required explicit user go-ahead since it writes real issues under the user's identity. Real bug found+fixed live: loose GitHub search API cross-matched other policies' issues, silently skipping 2 of 5; fixed via exact-title client-side matching. Correction: the '27 fetched/23 outside window' figures are a point-in-time snapshot that will not reproduce on re-run by construction (feed keeps growing), not an error.

tickets.title: Policy handbook generator from a tag
tickets.acceptance_gist: Generator against a tag produces a readable handbook covering every policy in that version; regenerating from a different tag reflects that version's set with nothing hand-maintained.
tickets.evidence_claimed: policy repo handbook/generate.sh <tag> (git show/git ls-tree only, no checkout); proven against two real signed tags (v1.0.1: 2 policies, blank pre-schema fields gracefully; v2.1.1: 3 policies, correctly picks up new policy). No generated HANDBOOK.md committed (would itself drift).
tickets.honesty_flags: Correction: generator's location/invocation is stale — extracted by real-estate ticket 05 into standalone handbook-generator repo with a changed invocation shape (generate.sh <policy-checkout-path> <tag>); policy repo's handbook/ dir is gone.

tickets.title: Agent plain-language summaries in the handbook
tickets.acceptance_gist: Each policy carries a plain-language summary derived from advisory metadata; summaries regenerate with handbook, stale summaries cannot ship; residual last-mile problem stated explicitly, no over-claim.
tickets.evidence_claimed: handbook/generate.sh <tag> --with-summaries using real claude -p headless calls per policy, run live against v1.0.1's two policies; content-hash cache (handbook/.cache/) + verify-fresh.sh proven live (deleted a cache entry -> STALE/exit1, regenerated -> OK/exit0).
tickets.honesty_flags: README explicitly frames this as 'a summary of the rationale a human wrote, not a substitute for a human deciding whether the policy still holds.' CI-wiring is a named residual gap needing a secret only the org owner can add. Wave-5 correction: generator location/invocation stale, same extraction as ticket 25, moved to handbook-generator repo with an added leading checkout-path arg.

thesis_or_destination: Not stated as one sentence in docs/adr/ itself; the ADRs repeatedly invoke 'the thesis' as an external referent. ADR-0001: 'the thesis prizes the git tag as the most legible, reviewable expression of "what is the policy and what version is it."' ADR-0002: 'the thesis's non-negotiable is the reviewed upgrade ("debate happens in pull requests, not exemption requests")'. ADR-0004: 'one versioned-dependency mechanism, one engine, governing both Kubernetes workloads and cloud resources at runtime. Closes the gap the talk admitted.' Recurring destination: policy as a versioned, signed dependency, enforced deterministically by one engine across multiple planes, changed only via reviewed human PRs, measured via layered ground truth including OSCAL attestation.

decisions.title: Transport: distribute versioned policy as signed git tags (keyless, gitsign)
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: Policy distributed as semver git tags signed keyless with gitsign, consumed via Flux GitRepository pinned on both tag and resolved commit SHA. Chosen over OCI+cosign because OCI's value was mostly working around a current Flux gap; OCI retained as north-star for attestations/SBOM.

decisions.title: Adoption cadence: pin exact versions everywhere, bump via reviewed Renovate PR
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: Every consumer pins an exact policy tag+commit SHA; new versions adopted only via reviewed, automerge:false Renovate PR everywhere. Rejects Flux live semver ranges as deleting the review gate.

decisions.title: Engine API: Kyverno CEL ValidatingPolicy, not the 2022 ClusterPolicy
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: Policies authored as Kyverno ValidatingPolicy (CEL) not deprecated ClusterPolicy. Multi-version coexistence corrected to matchConditions after live testing found objectSelector flattens across policies onto one shared webhook (last-reconciled wins).

decisions.title: Cloud/IaC plane: harvest ControlPlane's collie (cloud-as-CR), not Checkov
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: Cloud plane built by harvesting collie's OSCAL catalogue and policy intent as data; hand-authored CEL ValidatingPolicy governs Crossplane CRs via the same Kyverno engine. collie's generator, Lula wiring, bootstrap harness dropped.

decisions.title: Install & fleet layer: ControlPlane Flux Operator (FluxInstance + ResourceSet)
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: Flux installed/managed via ControlPlane's Flux Operator instead of vanilla flux bootstrap; cluster x version coexistence matrix expressed as a ResourceSet. Guardrail: thesis must remain vanilla-Flux-expressible.

decisions.title: Policy code is deterministic — no time-conditional state
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: No expiry/date-based CEL logic in policy bodies. 'Delete-if-undefended' realised as editorial PR, not mechanical date trigger; review metadata is advisory-only.

decisions.title: Governance: agent-assisted editorial review (the human layer the mea-culpa demands)
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: Human governance realised as editorial review supported by an AI/agent layer that surfaces business decisions as issues/PRs but never edits enforcement. Two in-text self-corrections retract earlier claims: demonstrator opens GitHub issues not PRs; no scoped GitHub App/token was ever set up, every write runs on full-access personal gh auth.

decisions.title: "Measurable" = layered ground-truth; PR-acceptance demoted to adoption velocity
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: Measurable pillar = four panels over four datasources (Flux revision, PolicyReports, OSCAL via C2P, Renovate PR state), not one PromQL join. PR-acceptance relabelled adoption velocity, not compliance proof. Phased: P1=revision+PolicyReports, OSCAL lands P2.

decisions.title: OSCAL attestation via Compliance-to-Policy (C2P), not Lula
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: OSCAL assessment-results produced by C2P's result2oscal from Kyverno PolicyReports; Lula dropped entirely (Lula 2 dropped OSCAL, lula1 unmaintained/redundant). Live KiND spike (2026-07-14) proved the mapping with a small jq shim.

decisions.title: Sunset: scheduled proposals, never scheduled application
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: A fleet array entry may carry a sunset date; on the date a machine opens a retirement PR that a human must merge. Enforced by allow_auto_merge:false and require-pr-gate. Extends ADR-0006's boundary: timed reminders ok, timed enforcement not.

decisions.title: Release gate: compute the bump, refuse a weaker declaration, no override
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: Publisher and adopter gates compute semver bump from observed verdict movement and refuse a weaker declared bump; never rewrite it. No override at any scope — would be the banned exemptions ledger by another name.

decisions.title: Composed artefact: self-signed by the adopter, reproducible from pinned parent SHAs, verified in CI
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: Composed policy set self-signed by the adopter using the same gitsign tag mechanism; parent digest is the already-pinned resolved commit SHA, not a new content hash.

decisions.title: The regulator publishes named baselines, the adopter selects one, and both key on the bare catalogue id
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: Regulator publishes named signed OSCAL baselines; adopter selects one, may add controls but never remove one. Exact-string bare id resolution. Estate selects MODERATE (285 recorded holes day one). New hole refuses composition; pre-existing hole recorded.

decisions.title: An unclaimed pod is caged, not denied; a governed namespace requires a claim at CREATE
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: Resolves contradiction: CONTEXT.md claimed the orphan guard denies unlabelled pods; committed guard actually skips them (correctly, or it would brick kube-system/Flux/Kyverno and break de-posture UPDATEs). Real hole closed by a new CREATE-only ValidatingPolicy on governed namespaces — specified here, not built here (platform's fifth named gap).

decisions.title: The proposer: the adopter runs it, in its own repo, and it opens the PR
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: Existing war-gamer becomes the tier-drift proposer; adopter runs it in its own repo on its own token and it now commits/pushes/opens the PR (previously stopped at the diff). No schedule exists anywhere — named blind spot for EOL drift. Deny-tier coercion-to-baseline bug recorded as a real platform defect.

decisions.title: A subclass never restates a mutate: the tier is the only knob, and only the proposer turns it
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: Restatement/strictness comparison applies only to ValidatingPolicy members; Mutating/GeneratingPolicy have no ladder so restating one is refused. Fixes a spike bug (validationActions written onto every member kind) and a resolver-key collision (silent overwrite).

decisions.title: A control claim belongs to whoever ships the implementation, and an adopter's own addition is an ordinary hole
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: A control is filled by a signed OSCAL claim from whoever ships the implementation (any party). An adopter-added control with no implementation is an ordinary new hole; adopter may never claim against another party's policy or remove a control it added.

decisions.title: The Namespace manifest is the governed declaration; the composed artefact carries no namespace list
decisions.status: accepted
decisions.gist: The governed:"true" label on each adopter's own signed Namespace manifest is the sole governed-scope declaration; composed artefact carries it only as advisory, re-derivable metadata. Composition refuses a new ungoverned namespace, records a pre-existing one.

A live KiND spike proving C2P result2oscal correctly maps Kyverno PolicyReports to OSCAL assessment-results, including a working jq shim for a report-shape mismatch — ADR-0009, spikes/c2p-validatingpolicy-oscal/
A release gate computing semver bump from observed verdict movement and refusing a weaker declared bump, at both publish and adoption time — ADR-0011
Composed multi-parent policy artefacts, self-signed by the adopter, reproducible byte-for-byte from pinned parent commit SHAs — ADR-0012

rejections_and_supersessions: ADR-0001: OCI+cosign 'Rejected as complexity introduced to dodge a Flux gap, not to serve the thesis. Retained as the north-star option.'
ADR-0001: 'Git tags + long-lived GPG keys (rejected)... reintroduces GPG key custody across a fleet.'
ADR-0002: Flux live semver ranges rejected: 'silently delete that review gate.' Per-environment/per-policy-class splits 'Recorded as a north-star option only.'
ADR-0003: ClusterPolicy rejected as a 'dying API'; ValidatingAdmissionPolicy 'rejected for the floor — it drops PolicyReports/mutation/generation and abandons the reference engine.'
ADR-0004: 'We do not inherit collie's generator, Lula wiring, or bootstrap.' collie's policies called 'a generated, static demo.'
ADR-0004/0009: 'defenseunicorns/lula is now Lula 2 — a SvelteKit/Express compliance-documentation web app... that deliberately dropped OSCAL... Lula is dropped entirely.'
ADR-0005: vanilla flux bootstrap rejected for the floor but 'retained as the documented fallback per the guardrail.'
ADR-0006: 'This supersedes the rejected expiry options (engine hard-expiry; class-aware auto-removal on a date)... none of them ship.'

ADR-0007: 'this originally said "opens PRs" -- the actual demonstrator... deliberately opens GitHub issues instead.' Second correction: 'the first correction's own wording... repeated the same overclaim... no scoped GitHub App or token was ever set up.'
ADR-0008: 'The headline shifts from the 2022 pitch ("compliance is a GitHub PR search away") to demonstrable control satisfaction with evidence... a deliberate departure from the talk's framing.'

ADR-0011: 'Trust the declared bump, test it after the fact (rejected — status quo)... That is post-hoc justification, not derivation.' 'An override on this gate is the same shape wearing a different label... That is the exemptions ledger this estate already deleted.'
ADR-0013: 'Refuse on any hole. Rejected: 285 holes on day one would deny the whole estate for ever. That is a wall, not a gate.'
ADR-0013: 'The cs-06b prototype's case-folding check is void... it must be rewritten.' 'The cs-06b prototype modelled it as a hypothetical nist v2.0.0 addition, and that modelling is superseded.'
ADR-0014: 'CONTEXT.md as written. Rejected on the facts above.' 'The locked-door claim is narrowed... The gate tier is an opt-in door, not the locked door CONTEXT.md claimed.'
ADR-0014: 'An exemption list for infrastructure namespaces. Rejected on the map's standing preference. Exemptions are banned.'
ADR-0015: 'platform runs it and opens PRs across orgs (Rejected)... no scoped app or token was ever set up. The estate should not invent one for this.'
ADR-0016: 'The spike had this defect and it is fixed... render() wrote spec.validationActions onto every member unconditionally... It is now guarded by kind.'
ADR-0016: 'The old resolver key overwrites in silence... That is luck, not design. A named gap in the spike, closed in the new loader.'
ADR-0016: 'Let the overlay declare a per-party tier floor... Rejected. A floor in the overlay is a verdict set by a declaration rather than by the £. That is the override this model does not have.'
ADR-0018: 'The composed artefact lists namespaces and the label is rendered from it (Rejected)... restates a signed fact in a second place.'
open_items: ADR-0001: on-cluster Flux-native gitsign gate blocked on fluxcd/source-controller#1068, tracked not blocking.
ADR-0001: signed attestations of the 'why' and SBOM deferred to the OCI north-star report.
ADR-0004: UK catalogue (NCSC CAF/GovAssure) can be added later, currently illustrative US NIST framing.
ADR-0007: non-technical human adoption of the handbook 'remains partly cultural and is named as a residual open problem'; the last-mile handbook itself is marked 'proposed — confirm'.
ADR-0009: C2P is pre-GA (v2.0.0-rc.1), pinned/vendored, 'track for GA.'
ADR-0013: MODERATE baseline starts at 285 recorded holes to be individually implemented or accepted.

ADR-0016: 'No new refusal reaches an adopter today... The rule is written before the first case, not after it.' Composition proven faithful but 'does not prove the twin matches what flux-operator renders in-cluster.'

notes: All 18 files carry 'status: accepted' with no other lifecycle states present. ADR-0007 uniquely contains two dated in-text self-corrections (2026-07-18, wave-1 and wave-2 audit) retracting its own earlier overclaims about the governance agent's write scope. ADR-0009 through ADR-0018 form a connected reasoning chain, each frequently correcting or narrowing an earlier ADR or CONTEXT.md (e.g. 0014 narrows CONTEXT.md's 'locked door' framing; 0016 fixes a spike bug discovered while writing the ADR). Several ADRs (0011,0013,0014,0015,0016,0018) describe defects found and fixed in the same commit as the ADR itself, so they read as combined decision+fix records. ADR-0013/14/15/16/17/18 reference an outside 'map' and numbered tickets (01, 03, 04, 13) living outside docs/adr/ that were not read as part of this group. No formal 'tickets' with id/title/status/acceptance/verify-command exist inside docs/adr/ itself; the closest is ADR-0009's build-precondition spike with a runnable path (spikes/c2p-validatingpolicy-oscal/), captured under claims_built rather than as a ticket.

thesis_or_destination: "Re-implement CNS's Policy as [Versioned] Code thesis on Flux CD — distributing organisational policy as a semantically-versioned, signed dependency, governed by a single Kyverno engine across both a Kubernetes workload plane and a Crossplane cloud plane, with reviewed (PR-gated) upgrades, multi-version runtime coexistence, ground-truth compliance, and an agent-assisted human-governance layer — proven reproducibly on KiND." (docs/PRD.md, one-line summary). PRD posture: "Faithful-to-intent build. A separate north-star report documents the fuller modern reference." README frames PRD.md as "the faithful-to-intent build, phased P1→P2→P3" and north-star-modern-reference.md as "the fuller modern reference the floor grows into."

decisions.title: Transport: signed git tags (gitsign, keyless), commit-SHA pinning
decisions.status: Referenced from PRD as binding; ADR file itself not in this group's paths
decisions.gist: Policy released as semver git tags signed keyless via gitsign (Sigstore/Fulcio/Rekor). Flux GitRepository pins spec.ref.tag AND spec.ref.commit. Known limitation accepted: Flux GitRepository.spec.verify is PGP-only, cannot verify gitsign — no Flux-native verified-source gate on the floor; verification runs in CI/at-merge pending fluxcd/source-controller#1068.

decisions.title: Adoption: pinned everywhere + Renovate PR; two axes independent
decisions.status: Referenced from PRD as binding; ADR file not in this group's paths
decisions.gist: Exact tags+commit pinned everywhere; new versions land only via reviewed CI-gated Renovate PR (automerge:false). Adoption cadence is independent of enforcement action. A single Renovate customManager (git-refs datasource) bumps every {tag,commit} pin, since Renovate's native flux manager can't maintain that pair.

decisions.title: Engine & policy authoring: Kyverno CEL ValidatingPolicy
decisions.status: Referenced from PRD as binding; ADR file not in this group's paths
decisions.gist: Policies are CEL ValidatingPolicy; validationActions is the enforcement axis (Audit=lane-keeping, Deny=gate), independent of adoption cadence; requires Kyverno >=1.18; the engine's HelmRelease is itself pinned and bumped via the same reviewed Renovate path.

decisions.title: Cloud plane: harvest collie, rebuild native
decisions.status: Referenced from PRD as binding; ADR file not in this group's paths
decisions.gist: Harvest controlplaneio/collie's IP (NIST 800-53r5 policy intent + OSCAL catalogue) rather than fork its toolchain (legacy ClusterPolicy generated via now-dropped Lula 1); hand-author CEL policies against current Crossplane v2 + AWS provider CRDs; collie's generator/Lula wiring/EKS-Terraform bootstrap dropped, not ported.

decisions.title: Multi-version coexistence: ResourceSet matrix; Operator is sugar not mechanism
decisions.status: Referenced from PRD as binding; ADR file not in this group's paths
decisions.gist: N GitRepository objects + nameSuffix collision-free objects + matchConditions CEL version self-scoping (not matchConstraints objectSelector) + workload opt-in label + fleet-held single {version,commit} array ranged over by ResourceSet templates. "The Operator is install/fleet sugar, not the mechanism."

decisions.title: Deterministic policy; editorial (not automated/timed) review and retirement
decisions.status: Referenced from PRD as binding; ADR file not in this group's paths
decisions.gist: No time-conditional logic in policy bodies. Dated/reviewed/removed-if-undefended is an editorial PR action — never automated or timed; orphan guard may start in Audit and promote to Deny only by editorial PR.

decisions.title: Carry, don't (yet) enforce, the why; agent governance boundary
decisions.status: Referenced from PRD as binding; ADR file not in this group's paths
decisions.gist: Advisory metadata is read by humans+agents only, never consumed by the engine. The agent governance layer never edits enforcement, only prompts humans via review PRs/issues; built as a bounded demonstrator (one signal source) plus a complete architectural spec.

decisions.title: Compliance / measurable: layered ground-truth dashboard
decisions.status: Referenced from PRD as binding; ADR file not in this group's paths
decisions.gist: One dashboard, four panels over four datasources (Flux revision, PolicyReports, OSCAL via C2P, Renovate PR state) joined by a shared cluster+policy-version template variable, not a PromQL join.

decisions.title: OSCAL emission via C2P result2oscal, not Lula
decisions.status: Referenced from PRD as binding; ADR file not in this group's paths
decisions.gist: C2P result2oscal normalises Kyverno PolicyReports (both planes) into OSCAL assessment-results, avoiding a second validation engine (why Lula was dropped). VP->report mapping proven by a spike, to be retired before P2. C2P is pre-GA (rc), pinned+vendored.

thesis_or_destination: From 03: "Treat policy as a versioned software dependency, not as a gate." Quote: "If policy is a dependency, then it should behave like one. It should have a version number. It should follow semantic versioning. It should live in a Git repository." Refined (mea culpa) position: "Policy should be lane keeping assist where lane keeping assist is appropriate... Policy should be a dependency — versioned, tested, consumed, and updated automatically — not a gate" but "Some policies belong at the gate... I want a locked door." From 20 (destination of this research group): "This document is Phase 1 — faithful expansion only... to expand CNS's 'Policy as [Versioned] Code' onto Flux primitives 1:1, NOT to redesign it." From 21: the companion "principal-engineer subtraction pass CNS asked for: 'research how to modernise (or better yet consider where it could be SIMPLIFIED).'" From 22: "A single de-duplicated, prioritised register of every open design decision raised by the faithful-mapping (20) and simplify/modernise (21) syntheses. Drives the requirements-grilling session before the PRD."

tickets.title: Research: cyber-risk quantification (FAIR and peers)
tickets.acceptance_gist: Provide concrete formulas, worked numbers, and a minimal reference implementation for a FAIR-style engine (LEF x Loss Magnitude via Monte Carlo over beta-PERT), plus appetite/tolerance bands mapping to Audit/Warn/Deny, and residual/waiver pricing maths.
tickets.evidence_claimed: A ~40-line numpy fair.py reference implementation (pert, simulate, summary, lec, control_value, portfolio_residual) with an inline __main__ self-check asserting mean ALE and VaR95 fall in expected bands against the canonical Kindly Ops worked example (LEF(2,4,9), LM(1k,4k,9k) -> mean ~£17k, VaR95 ~£31k) and Deny buys positive risk reduction (effectiveness > 0.8).
tickets.honesty_flags: Proposed/example implementation embedded in the research doc, not confirmed landed elsewhere in the repo. Explicitly descoped: TEF×Vulnerability decomposition, secondary-loss as its own simulation, cross-scenario correlation, a distribution-fitting UI. PERT λ fixed at 4, marked ponytail:. Section 4 separates 'done' vs 'aspirational' (cyber risk as an audited balance-sheet line item is explicitly aspirational).

tickets.title: Projecting Kyverno admission "posture" into a SPIRE workload identity
tickets.status: Research for the governance/security conference demo (no resolved/status header; feasibility-question framing).
tickets.acceptance_gist: Determine whether Kyverno admission-time policy posture can become an attested SPIRE SVID property gateable by Istio AuthorizationPolicy and OpenBao.
tickets.evidence_claimed: Verdict: 'Yes — feasible for a KinD demo, natively, with no custom SPIRE plugin.' Wiring: Kyverno mutate stamps a posture label -> ClusterSPIFFEID templates it into the SPIFFE URI path -> Istio principal-prefix match -> OpenBao bound_claims glob. Backed by citations to official SPIFFE/SPIRE/Istio/Kyverno/OpenBao docs; this is design/feasibility research, not implementation evidence.
tickets.honesty_flags: Self-flagged core caveat: posture is an admission-time snapshot; a stale workload keeps a 'current' SVID until a not-yet-built 'currency controller' (described only as 'even a 30-line CronJob') re-patches the label. 7 numbered honest gaps/risks listed, including a security-critical forgeability risk (pod label trust boundary) requiring a Kyverno validate rule not confirmed implemented, no native per-entry JWT claims, Istio prefix/suffix-only matching, OpenBao's lack of native SPIFFE auth, and bounded (not instant) revocation latency.

tickets.title: 18 — Human, device-trusted access to Kubernetes & infra (the "human carrier")
tickets.status: Research for the zero-trust governance conference demo. All web facts verified 2026-07-31.
tickets.acceptance_gist: Give humans phishing-resistant, device-trusted, per-session-RBAC, audited operational access to the KinD estate, consistent with existing SPIFFE/SPIRE and gitsign trust roots, using genuinely OSS tooling only.
tickets.evidence_claimed: Verdict: Teleport OSS disqualified (Device Trust and OIDC/SAML SSO confirmed Enterprise-only against Teleport's own docs). Recommends Pomerium Core + SPIRE tpm_devid + WebAuthn + optional Fleet/osquery, each claim cross-referenced to 25 primary vendor docs/repos dated 2026-07-31. Comparative research/recommendation, not a built-and-tested demo.
tickets.honesty_flags: Licensing traps section: Teleport Community binaries commercially restricted since v16 (no longer Apache-2.0 despite the name); HashiCorp Boundary is BSL 1.1 (not OSI-open) with k8s session recording still 'in progress'; Cloudflare/BeyondCorp/StrongDM/Twingate proprietary/SaaS. thesis_or_destination: "Make the estate real and let the existing mechanism prove itself against it. Five real app teams in five repos, with real stacks, deliberately mixed dependency hygiene, and one team owning the cloud-plane claims. Extract every reusable component into its own versioned, pinned repo... Close the gate's version cross-check hole. Give the CIO the forward-looking answers... Wire the live Renovate service in behind an org-level preset. Add follow-through tracking to the governance checkboxes without ever touching policy content. One new dashboard joins the two kinds of staleness — policy versions and app dependencies — into a single per-team estate view, which *strengthens* the core metaphor: a policy version is just another dependency." (spec.md). Born from show+tell demo feedback (2026-07-16) that exposed the prior faithful-floor epic's estate as "a cardboard cutout" (spec.md, Problem Statement).

decisions.title: Sunset as scheduled proposals, never scheduled application
decisions.status: done (ticket 02)
decisions.gist: A sunset: date lives on fleet array entries (adoption-scoped, never in the immutable release); dashboards show a countdown; the governance agent opens escalating issues as the date nears; on the date a machine opens a retirement PR that a human must merge. Nothing timed ever applies. States explicitly it extends ADR-0006's boundary deliberately (ADR-0006 forbids timed enforcement changes; ADR-0002 already sanctions machine-opened PRs — invariant is "never automerged", not "never machine-initiated").

thesis_or_destination: map.md Destination: "A **conference-grade talk** (first-class **Marp** deck) that lands one thesis — *governance should be a **proportionate, informed response to quantified risk**, and versioning the whole chain from risk-appetite to evidence is how you keep that proportionality honest, current, and provable* — **backed by a fully-real, refactored demo estate** where every claim is demo-live, not narrated. ... Done when: the talk spec (spine, claims, deck) is locked **and** the estate is refactored so nothing in the talk is faked or hinted." the-whole-model.md Thesis: "Governance is a **proportionate, informed, continuously re-tuned response to quantified risk** — and versioning the whole chain from risk-appetite to evidence, with **every actor attestable**, is how proportionality stays honest and current as the world moves." Tightest form: "policy is a versioned dependency — and that one dependency is the whole governance surface." spec.md Solution: a "~35–40 min, touring" Marp deck plus "the **delivery refactor**: a fresh six-org estate (`policy-as-versioned-{platform,driftwood,tuppence,ludlow,nist,ico}`), one KinD cluster per institution, where every claim is demo-live rather than narrated."

decisions.gist: Not one org but a six-org topology, all live, all under `policy-as-versioned-*`: platform + institutions driftwood (e-comm PCI+GDPR) / tuppence (fintech FCA+PCI+GDPR) / ludlow (US health HIPAA) + regulators nist (real 800-53 OSCAL) and ico (real public fine magnitudes repackaged). All three institutions fully live; the prefix is the impersonation guardrail; existing policy-as-versioned-flux archived at the END of migration. Portability/proportionality proven by comparison — same encrypt-at-rest control Audit in driftwood, Deny in ludlow because a HIPAA breach costs ~8x a retail one.

decisions.title: Architecture skeleton & Flux's load-bearing role
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 08
decisions.gist: Keep Kyverno ValidatingPolicy (CEL). Flux load-bearing in six named jobs (ResourceSet fan-out, signed GitRepository provenance, prune-on-retire, drift-heal, dependsOn/health ordering, notification event spine). Exemptions = git ledger entry -> rendered PolicyException with Flux prune + cleanup.kyverno.io/ttl. Shift-left = ±1 version skew off the ResourceSet array. Crossplane stays the cloud plane. 'Sunset' dissolved into lifecycle/EOL risk fed from endoflife.date. Everything built, no cuts.

decisions.title: Shift-left policy-version compatibility (dev + CI, before deploy)
decisions.status: Type: prototype / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 02
decisions.gist: Cluster advertises supported policy versions via the ResourceSet array; dev/CI reads it kubectl-style (±1 skew) and `kyverno apply` runs the target version's real action offline, so an Audit->Deny flip is caught in CI before merge. That CI catch IS the shift-left beat. No dedicated dev cluster — 'a deploy-time fail even to dev is unheard-of' stays narrated.

decisions.title: Risk → proportionality model (appetite in £ → control strength → residual)
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 01, 07
decisions.gist: FAIR (frequency x severity) -> ALE + VaR95 + TVaR with a risk load; proportionality = the four risk-financing moves (avoid / reduce / transfer / retain); five versioned feed threads; calibration via Bühlmann credibility theory; £ framed as economic/risk-based capital. Appetite shape locked: ludlow strictest (Deny-heavy), driftwood loosest (Audit-heavy), tuppence toward-strict. Exact £, bands and per-institution threat registers DERIVE during build.

decisions.title: Conditional policy, not exemptions (residual risk of permissive branches)
decisions.status: Type: prototype / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 02, 04
decisions.gist: Exemptions dissolved into conditional policy — 'you may X if conditions C' (team/location/attestation/data-class/time-bound) in Kyverno CEL, versioned like any rule, applied uniformly. Residual of each permissive branch feeds the FAIR £. Mechanically still a git ledger entry -> rendered PolicyException (Flux prune + ttl backstop), and the ledger entry generates the OSCAL risk/POA&M object. Reframed 2026-07-23 by the human.

decisions.title: Balance-sheet quantification (residual → £ → insurance/valuation), built real
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 04, 07, 09
decisions.gist: The balance sheet is the NARRATED close, not a live beat: lead with insurance (underwriters price the same controls, ±20-40% premium), land on the board, valuation one-lined. Still built real (economic/risk-based capital, TVaR + risk load, reserving line) and the moving-£ loop is demonstrated live. Update 2026-07-23: the number is Total Cost of Risk = retained residual + cost of controls in force (incl. dynamic cages) + risk transfer (premiums).

decisions.title: RESEARCH: cyber-risk quantification (FAIR and peers)
decisions.status: Type: research / Status: resolved / Blocked by: —
decisions.gist: FAIR taxonomy directly implementable: (min,mode,max) triples -> beta-PERT (lambda=4) -> Monte Carlo 10k+ -> ALE (mean), VaR95, loss-exceedance curve. 'Audit->Deny' is a number: £ a control buys = ALE_warn - ALE_deny, judged against tolerance bands. Insurance underwriting prices the same controls (MFA ~15-25%, EDR ~10-20%, backups ~10-15%) = external validation. Residual = Inherent x (1 - control effectiveness); total residual = ALE_deny·covered + ALE_warn·exempted. Inputs are versioned triples so the risk number versions with the policy.

decisions.title: RESEARCH: enforcement engine & exemption/shift-left options under a Flux anchor
decisions.status: Type: research / Status: resolved / Blocked by: —
decisions.gist: Keep Kyverno ValidatingPolicy (CEL, policies.kyverno.io/v1, >=1.18) — wins on all three criteria; switching buys nothing under a Flux anchor. PolicyException is first-class but has NO native expiry — closed via ledger entry + Flux prune (primary) + cleanup.kyverno.io/ttl (backstop); requires enablePolicyException + exceptionNamespace in the Kyverno HelmRelease. Alternatives judged and rejected: OPA/Gatekeeper (no expiring exception CR, Rego tax), Kubewarden (Wasm fragmentation), native VAP (no official offline CLI, north-star only), jsPolicy (dormant since ~2024 — exclude). Flux load-bearing in six real jobs; image automation unused, 'don't invent a use'. Shift-left = ±1 window (stale-by-one warn, two block).

decisions.title: RESEARCH: OSCAL risk / POA&M / accepted-risk for the up-flow
decisions.status: Type: research / Status: resolved / Blocked by: —
decisions.gist: OSCAL carries the risk half natively: `risk` is a first-class assessment-layer assembly shared verbatim between assessment-results and POA&M; NIST's own example ships status:deviation-approved + remediation type:accept + deadline. Ledger row -> one risk with related-observations pointing at the C2P not-satisfied observation = clean 1:1. Magnitude is qualitative by design (facet value is a string, no native numeric/money datatype) so the £ attaches as a facet under our own system URI, the same idiom CVSS uses. Current C2P result2oscal emits only observations + findings and NEVER instantiates a risk.

decisions.title: Regulator-as-upstream-dependency: machine-readable control & penalty artifacts
decisions.status: Type: prototype / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 02
decisions.gist: Regulators are versioned, signed upstream dependencies. nist = real OSCAL controls (native). ico penalties = a small bespoke signed versioned schema (regime -> violation-type -> fine formula/cap) feeding FAIR loss-magnitude directly, explicitly NOT force-fit into OSCAL. endoflife.date EOL and CVE feeds ride the same pattern; a regulator change arrives as a reviewable PR. Schema shape + ingestion are build-work.

decisions.title: Multi-org topology & shared-tooling inheritance (incl. the archive-flux migration)
decisions.status: Type: prototype / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 02

One real KinD cluster per institution (three, separate). platform consumed by each institution as a pinned, signed dependency (linting config-base pattern one level up). Archive policy-as-versioned-flux as the last step.

decisions.title: War-gaming & AI policy-PR agent (the loop-closer)
decisions.status: Type: prototype / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 04, 14
decisions.gist: governance-agent (ADR-0007, today CVE->issue) evolves into a war-gaming policy-PR proposer: collect five feeds -> war-game scenarios against current controls -> on proportionality drift open a policy PR with re-tuned controls. Proposes, never disposes — rides human review + PR-gate version cross-check + gitsign->Rekor + versioned distribution. Scenarios AI-generated + human seed, results logged back as calibration evidence. Agent code + scenario library are build-work.

decisions.title: Wardley mapping as the strategic (anticipation) layer

Map updates are commits with attestable provenance. Generator + market-intel ingestion are build-work.

decisions.title: Enforcement response gradient — proportionate graded outcomes, not binary admit/deny
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: None (extends resolved 02, 04, 05, 06)
decisions.gist: Enforcement is a proportionate graded response. (A) self-envelope: Kyverno mutate+generate cages a workload's own runtime by degree (throttled CPU/mem/IOPS/net, heavier WAF sidecar, dropped caps, read-only-fs, eviction priority); Deny is the bottom rung. (B) posture-as-identity: the admitted policy version becomes a claim on the workload's SPIFFE/SPIRE SVID gating Istio AuthorizationPolicy and OpenBao secret issuance. Economics = TCoR; the war-gamer picks fix/cage/transfer/deny by TCoR. Abstraction = tiers over dials. Scope = build everything, estate-wide, gating density follows proportionality. Flagship live beat = customer-accounts-reset (tuppence).
decisions.depends_on_bare_agree: Two owner interventions recorded as bare directives without wording: the 'Correction (human)' that trust must never earn loose, and 'Scope = build everything, estate-wide (human)'.

decisions.title: Research: Kyverno → SPIRE posture projection (the non-trodden hand-off)
decisions.status: Type: research / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 16
decisions.gist: Feasible on KinD natively, no custom SPIRE plugin. Posture lives in the SPIFFE ID PATH, not a claim: Kyverno mutate stamps a posture.<org>/version label at admission -> one ClusterSPIFFEID whose spiffeIDTemplate bakes posture into the SVID URI -> spire-controller-manager reconciles <=10s. Istio gates source.principals prefix; OpenBao via jwt role bound_claims_type=glob; short-TTL (~5m) JWT-SVIDs. Forces two new components: a currency controller (posture is otherwise an admission snapshot) and a posture-label trust-boundary (else forgeable). Head-start: ControlPlane getting-started-spire-openbao.

decisions.title: Human & device identity — completing the zero-trust actor picture
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: None (extends 16)
decisions.gist: Posture-as-identity generalises to three actor classes — workload, human, device — under one policy on one attestation root (SPIFFE + gitsign/Rekor). Human: gitsign keyless already real for supply chain; operational access via Pomerium Core (Apache-2.0, OIDC + WebAuthn), gated proportionally. Device/EUD: SPIRE tpm_devid device SPIFFE IDs on the same root; Mac Secure-Enclave WebAuthn key is the genuine live hardware root; Windows + Linux EUDs built and demoed on UTM vTPM VMs, narrated as virtual (emulated EK). Carrier is NOT Teleport.
decisions.depends_on_bare_agree: The carrier-research section records 'Awaiting: human confirm + the Mac/TPM fidelity call'; the later Answer records the resolution but no owner wording is quoted.

decisions.title: Research: human+device access carrier — is Teleport the mature best-in-class, or is there better?
decisions.status: Type: research / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 18
decisions.gist: Teleport OSS = wrong pick: Device Trust is Enterprise-only (verbatim in docs), OIDC/SAML connectors Enterprise-only (Community = GitHub-only), and Community binaries are commercially restricted (<100 emp / <$10M rev since v16). Recommended: Pomerium Core (Apache-2.0) in front of the KinD API server + SPIRE tpm_devid issuing a TPM-rooted SPIFFE ID to the laptop; Fleet/osquery (MIT) as spoofable software posture. Field rejected: Boundary (BSL), Cloudflare/StrongDM/Twingate (proprietary SaaS), Tailscale (proprietary control plane).

decisions.title: It's all the policy — one artifact, five projections (2026-07-23)
decisions.status: recorded synthesis (no explicit status line)
decisions.gist: There are no subsystems — there is one artifact, the policy (versioned, signed, attestable); everything else is a projection of it or a function around it. policy@version determines admission, runtime envelope, identity, reach, entitlement. 'Exemptions' are recast as documented operating decisions; the OSCAL up-flow is the formal decision record; versioning is the decision history.

decisions.title: The talk's spine + demonstrable-core vs narrated-vision (Locked 2026-07-23)

Breach-cost is the cold open and balance-sheet the close — both narrated. Touring implies reproducible-on-a-laptop (idempotent, offline-safe, resettable) and audience-modular.

thesis_or_destination: This is a research corpus (not a decision/build tracker) feeding the org digital-twin project: modelling an organisation as a versioned Wardley/knowledge graph, sensing weak signals, pricing risk and opportunity in a single currency, and validating the whole thing against real-world backtests. Per twin-wardley-horizon-sota.md: "The twin = the graph we already have... a versioned knowledge graph of the estate, projected as Wardley maps, nudged by STEEP-classified weak signals that propagate along dependency edges, and replayed / fast-forwarded through git history for scenario what-if." Per blind-spots-fable.md, the underlying worry driving several of these research tracks: "every loop in this system — validation, calibration, falsification, the quality yardstick itself — currently closes through the same single mind. A twin whose ground truth, detector, scenarios, evaluation, and standard of success all come from one builder is not a falsifiable system with a synthetic substrate; it is a mirror with extra steps."

decisions.title: Flagship org selection, wave 1: LEGO + portfolio (ARM, Maersk, Nokia)
decisions.status: SUPERSEDED by wave 2 (see below); recorded as this file's own recommendation, then contradicted by its own contrarian-challenge section
decisions.gist: Ranked 24 OSINT candidate orgs by backtest_suitability/OSINT depth/comprehensibility/risk-breadth/entropy and recommended LEGO as flagship with ARM, Maersk, Nokia as portfolio. The file's own appended 'Contrarian challenge' section then attacks this pick as circular (LEGO's ground truth is 'the winner's memoir'), proposes Carillion or Ferrari instead, and flags an ethics problem (LEGO's aggressive brand enforcement + a living family).

decisions.title: Flagship/backtest re-scoping, wave 2: Netflix flagship, Enron backtest, corrected for temporal resolution
decisions.status: Recommendation stated, then substantially undercut by its own 'Wave-2 contrarian challenge' at the end of the same file
decisions.gist: Corrects wave 1 for ignoring 'temporal resolution' (public market cadence). Re-ranks living orgs: Netflix (flagship, composite 8.5) beats LEGO (re-scored 4 once private-company illiquidity is priced in). For the collapsed-firm backtest slot, ranks Enron top (composite 9.2) with Wirecard close second (9.0), Carillion/Lehman tied third (8.7). The file's own contrarian pass then argues Enron's adversarial ladder is 'half-retrospective' and parametrically contaminated (LLM training data already contains the SPE names/verdict), and recommends restructuring to 'Carillion primary backtest, Enron as contamination control, NMC Health replacing or joining Wirecard as the low-contamination second key.'

decisions.title: Opportunity-case backtest roster (ticket 19), responding to a push/pull decision made in 'ticket 13'
decisions.status: Recommendation made; file states baseline finding is negative ('No. Not one of them [meets the collapse bar], and the reason is structural')
decisions.gist: Assesses 14 candidate 'opportunity seized/missed' cases against the same evidence-ladder rigor used for the collapse roster (Carillion, Enron, Wirecard, NMC Health, Kodak). Recommends adding DSV/Panalpina and Albemarle/Rockwood (seized) and Royal Mail, Morrisons, RWE (missed), plus three explicit 'controls, not scored cases' (AstraZeneca hindsight trap, Sanofi inverse trap, Ørsted contamination dial). Concludes opportunity cases can never meet the collapse bar because there is no short-side/regulatory-disclosure/forced-post-mortem instrument for successes, so they must enter as bias-instrumentation, not capability validation.

decisions.title: Google TabFM (ticket 16) — REJECT for all of this project's quantitative needs
decisions.status: VERDICT: REJECT (with one narrow, non-load-bearing exception that is itself dominated by cheaper tools)
decisions.gist: TabFM's regression head is a scalar MLP, architecturally incapable of emitting a predictive distribution needed for PERT triples / heavy-tailed severity / TVaR; its preprocessing z-scores and ±4σ-clips exactly the tail the risk engine needs. Its only genuine advantage (trained solely on synthetic SCM data, so parametric-contamination-resistant) doesn't help because the project's contamination exposure is in the context data and the LLM substrate generator, not the predictor. Recommends running it only as an unpriced null baseline against LightGBM/TabPFN-3 co-baselines, one day, then closing permanently.

decisions.title: Prediction markets (ticket 17) — narrow signal source, co-registered calibration benchmark only
decisions.status: Recommended position for the ticket (section 11), not a bare agree
decisions.gist: Verdict table: live signal source = 'Yes — narrow'; aggregate Brier-score external calibration benchmark = 'No' (incomparable question sets); co-registered question-by-question benchmark = 'Yes — genuinely valuable but tests a different capability' (general world-forecasting, not the org-twin's causal machinery, so 'the circularity hole is not closed by this'). Recommends a world-layer connector (30–70c band, two independent venues, weight by trader count) plus a blind co-registered forecast book scored with log score + Metaculus-style peer score/coverage, and explicitly recommends NOT building an internal prediction market.

decisions.title: State-of-the-art risk/threat modelling verdict — FAIR skeleton kept, four disciplines added
decisions.status: Bottom line up front / final 'What we should actually build on' section
decisions.gist: Keeps the FAIR (Factor Analysis of Information Risk) factor-tree structure as sound, but declares the prior attempt ('hand-asserted FAIR triples with no calibration and no back-testing') to be 'astrology with a Monte-Carlo engine bolted on.' Mandates four additions: Hubbard calibrated estimation, Bühlmann–Straub credibility blending, empirical heavy-tailed loss data (Cyentia IRIS/DBIR) with Pareto/GPD tails, and back-testing. Names risk matrices/heat-maps and black-box CRQ scores as 'snake-oil.'

decisions.title: Twin engine architectural seam — one loop over the existing versioned graph
decisions.status: Recommended design ('Practical seam for our engine' section), presented as the researcher's own synthesis, not an owner-ratified ADR
decisions.gist: Recommends deriving the twin from the estate's existing GitHub-org dependency graph rather than building a new modelling tool; storing Wardley maps as OWM DSL and reusing the installed /arckit:wardley* skills as reasoning passes; treating horizon-scanning signals as STEEP-tagged and bound to graph components via LLM/human interpretation; propagating change via graph traversal + climatic-pattern rules (no ML); and using git history itself as the temporal spine for rewind/play/fast-forward.

decisions.title: arckit automation seam for scheduled Wardley refresh and what-if sweeps

notes: This directory is a pure research/scoping corpus, not a decision-tracker or build-tracker in the ticket-tracker sense used elsewhere in the project (no 'Status: OPEN/CLOSED/RESOLVED' ticket headers). Its content is nonetheless heavily decision-shaped: several files are literally 'pick one flagship' or 'accept/reject this technology' analyses with explicit verdicts, so they are reported above under both decisions and tickets depending on shape. Two files (flagship-osint-scoping.md and flagship-osint-scoping-wave2.md) each contain a self-contradicting structure: a primary recommendation followed by an appended adversarial 'contrarian challenge' section (evidently written by a different reviewer persona) that substantially attacks the file's own headline pick. A reviewer relying only on each file's top-line 'Recommendation' section would miss that the file itself later reverses or heavily qualifies that recommendation. As of these files, no later document in this directory reconciles the two waves' conflicting Netflix+Enron vs Netflix+Carillion-primary recommendations into one final answer. blind-spots-fable.md and misuse-catalogue-fable.md are both explicitly adversarial/red-team review documents ('role: divergent reviewer', 'Written by someone who has not seen your code and does not want to') critiquing a design ('the twin', 'the settled framing', 'your eight entries [misuse catalogue]') that is NOT itself present in this research/ directory — they reference and critique an external map.md and an existing misuse catalogue that must live elsewhere (likely .scratch/twin/ or .scratch/twin/issues/). Their findings are therefore about a design this inventory cannot independently verify was ever changed in response. Confidence ratings ('high'/'medium'/'speculative') are used self-referentially throughout blind-spots-fable.md and misuse-catalogue-fable.md as an internal severity/certainty marker by the reviewer-author, not as any kind of externally verified score — worth flagging to a drift reviewer as author-asserted confidence, not measured confidence. prediction-markets.md is unusually disciplined about sourcing hygiene, tagging nearly every claim [reported]/[inferred]/[probe] — this is the strongest evidentiary file in the group and is worth treating as a template for how the rest of the twin's evidence-grading ladder (referenced but not defined in this directory) should look. tabfm-assessment.md and risk-threat-sota.md both converge independently on the same conclusion — that the project's core difficulty is calibrated inference under sparse/heavy-tailed data, not supervised tabular prediction — which is corroborating rather than duplicative. Two files (opportunity-cases.md and flagship-osint-scoping-wave2.md) both independently invoke the same methodological move: pairing a 'contaminated' (famous, LLM-memorised) case with a 'clean' comparator at matched evidence density to produce a 'memorisation leakage discount dial' (Ørsted/RWE pair mirroring the Enron/NMC pair) — this is a recurring, load-bearing design pattern across the group worth a reviewer's attention as a single idea appearing twice, not two separate ideas. No file in this directory carries an explicit date-of-last-update banner beyond its 'Date:' header (all clustered 2026-08-04 to 2026-08-05, with arckit-capability-map.md noting its own arckit version snapshot 'at investigation time (2026-08-04)') — no staleness markers or superseded-banners are present except the wave1/wave2 relationship already noted.

thesis_or_destination: "Be careful to not allow scope to drop in this and prematurely declare things as done, and make sure we're prepared to always change our code and never be married to previous investments." (00-constitution.md, 'The standing guard'). Structurally: 'A single number ends a conversation; a map sustains one — the point of the artefact is to be argued with, distanced from the human stories and the emotion, so terminating the argument would destroy its function,' expressed as five refusals to collapse plurality (competing world models, rival causal accounts, multiple forecasts, trade-off curve never a verdict, contestability as primary workflow).
