decisions.title: Is "COTS" the boundary, or is it "can we change the pod spec"?
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: The axis is "can we change the pod spec," defined by its remedy: wrap it or shim it, never exempt, never deny. The population is mostly the platform's own infrastructure (five unlabelled third-party charts: SPIRE, Istio, OpenBao, Pomerium, Dex, plus flux-system/git-server) — the platform's own infra is in scope and is the leading case. Institution owns the risk and the £; platform owns the mechanism.

decisions.title: Where does the shim sit: procurement, build, or admission?
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 01
decisions.gist: Three layered sources across the lifecycle: wrapper (packaging time, makes the product a real pinned signed dependency), procurement record (selection time, carries the declared version), and SPIFFE identity (runtime, checkable). A platform-side allow-list mapping identity to version at admission was explicitly rejected as an unearned compliance claim about uninspected software.

decisions.title: What does compliance mean when the vendor image cannot comply?
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 01
decisions.gist: Compliance is achieved by the cage, not the image; the composite complies — already true in code via cage-tier.yaml. Conditional policy decides admission, the tier decides tightness, and residual risk lands in the institution's own band but tagged. Surfaced a new idea: COTS can outsource risk via vendor recourse, which the £ engine cannot yet express (spun into ticket 04).

decisions.title: Vendor recourse is a second transfer channel the £ engine cannot express
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 03
decisions.gist: One move, two instruments: transfer gains a counterparty dimension (carrier or vendor) rather than becoming a fifth move. Vendor recourse is zero-up-front but uncertain/slow/capped recovery, evidence-graded and fails closed (nothing below "reviewed and enforceable" earns credit, capped at contract cap, solvency a live input). Terms live on the procurement record. The exemption ledger, offered as an option for where terms could live, is banned outright here too.

decisions.title: Remove the exemption ledger, and let the cage produce its evidence
decisions.status: Type: task / Status: done / Blocked by: 04
decisions.gist: The exemption ledger (a live ResourceSet rendering PolicyException per entry, with render-exemption.py, verify-exemption.sh, and one entry EXC-2026-001 exempting legacy-till) is deleted as a banned carve-out concept, despite the ledger's own good arguments (scoped/priced/expiring/versioned/owned) being explicitly overruled. Replaced by the cage producing the OSCAL risk object itself (cage.py's oscal_risk()), sequenced before deletion so the OSCAL up-flow beat retains its input.

thesis_or_destination: map.md Destination: "A rigorous, comprehensive **digital twin of an organisation** and an **anticipatory strategic-intelligence engine**: it senses *any* signal — external (quantum, memory cost, AI-model access, sanctions, East–West realignment, climate, supply-chain, M&A) and internal (people, morale, knowledge concentration, comp, working patterns) — maps it onto the org's Wardley/dependency landscape, **war-games the what-ifs (fast-forward · rewind · play)**, prices every impact *and every candidate response* in **one £ risk currency**, and recommends the **cheapest proportionate response wherever it lives** — an HR lever, a security control, a strategic play. Versioned, attestable governance is *one enactment arm*, not the point." Also: "Plan the whole thing to full ambition — everything is modelled. The demo scope is worked backwards from the plan, later." and "Built **skills-first, from basics**, on **real risk modelling and real Wardley** — nothing inherited from the toy prior." Done when: "the whole is charted comprehensively (all workstreams, seams, and explicit acceptance criteria), grounded in real methodology, with a worked-backwards demo slice — such that a build could start any track without re-deciding its basis." spec.md restates the solution as "A **digital twin of an organisation** — a typed, git-versioned knowledge graph spined on the Wardley value chain — plus an **anticipatory engine** that runs over it", with four distinguishing properties: "It is a weather forecast", "It can be proved wrong, and the proof is structural", "It treats contamination as a first-class threat", "It is an artefact to argue with, not an oracle". Spec header: "Status: ready-for-agent / Source: `.scratch/twin/map.md` (`wayfinder:map`, decision-complete 2026-08-05) and its 22 resolved tickets. / Scope: **the whole system.** Each resolved ticket's full acceptance criteria remain the yardstick."

decisions.title: The subject & purpose — who is this for, and which organisation gets twinned?
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: RESOLVED (2026-08-04) / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: Subject = a fictitious org with an AI-synthesised noisy operational/behavioural substrate carrying planted weak signals of known ground truth, realism grounded in cross-sector OSINT; ONE flagship at maximum depth plus a portfolio of shallower orgs, each depth-upgradable on its own track, with N orgs + a per-org depth grade in the data model. Purpose priority: magnum opus > shippable product > research reference implementation > advisory persuasion; success = coverage + runnable + honest + legible, each workstream carrying its own ACs. A later refinement splits the flagship into a REAL public-history strategic spine (the backtest ground truth) plus a SYNTHETIC behavioural substrate.
decisions.depends_on_bare_agree: Answers recorded as option letters with substantive elaboration ('Subject = (b) a fictitious org...'; 'Purpose priority (highest first): (d) > (c) > (a) > (b)') — letters present but not bare.

decisions.title: RESEARCH: state of the art — quantified risk & threat modelling
decisions.status: Type: research / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: Keep the FAIR skeleton (LEF x LM -> PERT leaves -> Monte-Carlo -> loss-exceedance curve; Open FAIR, not a vendor black box) and add calibrated estimation (Hubbard), empirical heavy-tailed anchoring (Cyentia IRIS / DBIR / NetDiligence; lognormal body + Pareto/GPD tail), credibility theory (Bühlmann–Straub) and back-testing. Threat modelling (STRIDE, attack trees, MITRE ATT&CK) grounds frequencies; aggregate with copulas; report TVaR not VaR. Rejects risk matrices, arithmetic on ordinal/CVSS scores, black-box single-number CRQ.

decisions.title: RESEARCH: state of the art — org digital twins, Wardley automation & horizon scanning
decisions.status: Type: research / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: A digital twin of an organisation is best built as a live knowledge graph + ontology + feedback loop, not a simulator; vendors mirror the present well and simulate the future badly. Wardley gives the shape (value-chain dependency graph + evolution scalar + climate/doctrine/gameplay lenses) with OWM DSL maps-as-code plus the installed arckit skills. Horizon scanning = STEEP-tagged weak signals interpreted against the model (Hiltunen 'future sign'); git history IS the temporal spine — branch-per-scenario + map-diff gives fast-forward/rewind/play.

decisions.title: RESEARCH: the arckit toolkit — capabilities & Claude Code wiring
decisions.status: Type: research / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: arckit 6.7.5 is a 73-command governance harness over a machine-readable artefact graph; Wardley D/K/R maths is deterministic and recomputable; /arckit:impact (reverse-dependency blast-radius) and /arckit:build --refresh (resumable, SHA-256-hashed, DAG-cascading refresh) already exist and are inherited. Genuine net-new is a scenario object {baseline, moves[], drivers[]}. Caveats shaping the seams: impact is console-only with no history to diff, £/risk deltas are model-authored prose not formulas, refresh assumes one repo while this is an org of repos.

decisions.gist: Modelling = CERT Critical Pathway to Insider Risk for the features wrapped in FAIR for the £; MICE(S); ~80% of malicious insiders acted on a workplace grievance so peer-relative disgruntlement is the highest-signal feature; levers (least-privilege, JIT, SoD, UEBA) map onto FAIR factors so pay-rise-vs-hardening is computable; bus-factor runs in parallel and interacts. Guardrail for real deployment: UK GDPR + DPA 2018 + ICO 2023 guidance, legitimate interests + documented LIA (never consent), mandatory DPIA, advisory-only (Art. 22), no special-category inference (Art. 9), Equality Act bias testing. Synthetic data means the demo is exempt.

decisions.title: Research: Google TabFM — real reduction in ML build, or hype?
decisions.status: Type: research / Status: RESOLVED (2026-08-05) — **VERDICT: REJECT**. See research/tabfm-assessment.md / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: REJECT for all six analytical needs. Decisive: TabFM's regression head is a scalar MLP so it is architecturally incapable of a predictive distribution (no PERT triples, no GPD tail, no TVaR), and the shipped preprocessing z-scores the target and clips features at ±4σ, destroying exactly the heavy tail the risk engine measures. TabPFN-3 kept the distributional head TabFM dropped. It passes only the contamination pillar (synthetic-SCM pretraining), which was never binding; weights are non-commercial-licensed with no technical report; the narrow surviving use is dominated by LightGBM/TabPFN-3 at ~1/40th compute. Framing conclusion: these are inference and calibration problems, not tabular-prediction problems.

decisions.title: Research: prediction markets (Polymarket et al.) as signal + calibration benchmark
decisions.status: Type: research / Status: RESOLVED (2026-08-05) — see research/prediction-markets.md
decisions.gist: Narrow yes on both. Signal: consume price MOVES as dated world-layer events, never price LEVELS as probabilities. Benchmark: only co-registered forecasting (same question, same timestamp, blind emission); aggregate Brier comparison rejected outright because Brier is a property of a (forecaster, question set) pair. Co-registration is contamination-proof by construction but tests the forecaster, not the org-twin causal layer, so the circularity critique stays OPEN. Coverage is brutal: ~1 of 10 scenario families, 0% of the per-org overlay. Favourite–longshot bias rejects unbiasedness in every subsample including the highest-volume, worst in the deep tail. Beyond ticket: corporate prediction markets beat their experts by up to 25% MSE and were killed anyway; play money is within 1-5pp of real.

notes:
1) This group is 22 decision/research tickets plus a map and a spec at 'ready-for-agent'. It contains NO build record: every twin capability described is prospective, and spec.md says outright 'the twin is greenfield'. A drift review should treat all 'claims_built' entries here as either inherited arckit facts or map/spec insertions made later by the build effort.

2) Status-line honesty is mostly disciplined, with three exceptions worth checking: (a) ticket 06 is headed RESOLVED yet all six ACs remain unchecked '[ ]' and it still lists four unresolved verification items plus 'NMC Health ... Needs a verification pass before anchoring scores'; (b) ticket 11's sensor-gameability AC is ticked '[x]' while its own text says the position is deferred and 'remain a known, recorded gap'; (c) tickets 10 and 15 correctly use '[~]' partial markers and say so in their status lines.

3) map.md and spec.md have been edited AFTER the decision phase with build-era facts, so they are not pure decision-time documents. map's 'Not yet specified' now says ticket 15's sensor set and ticket 10's threat-model/misuse items are 'closed — build ticket 82 / 83' with concrete file paths, and spec user story 45 carries an inline '(Build ticket 39 finding: ...)' that NARROWS a decision-group choice — Wirecard, selected in ticket 06 as part of the low-contamination suite, is reclassified at build time as a second contamination 'high' case, leaving Carillion + NMC Health as 'this story's actual low-notoriety pair'. Ticket 06 itself was never updated to match.

4) Counts agree: map.md's 'Decisions so far' lists 22 entries, spec.md says '22 resolved tickets', and the issues directory holds exactly 22 files. But the map's index is ordered by resolution date rather than number (15 appears after 17, 18 after 19), which can read as gaps on a quick scan.

5) Ticket 01 has no acceptance-criteria checklist at all — it predates the AC convention used from ticket 06 onward. Tickets 02-05 (research) also have no checklists.

6) Several decisions are recorded as bare option letters from the owner with the rationale supplied by the writer — most notably ticket 22 Q1 '(b) AND (c), SEQUENCED TO CONCLUDE IN (a)', ticket 11 Q1 'b, then c', ticket 10 Q2 whose whole recorded human rationale is 'we need to demo it', ticket 10 Q4 '(a) ACCEPTED AS NOISE FOR NOW', and ticket 15 Q3 'human reviewed ... nothing missing from the table'. Where the owner spoke at length the quotes are substantive (ticket 09 Q1 on perspectival £, ticket 12 Q3b on the actionability horizon, ticket 14 Q2b on CI signing, ticket 20 Q2b the standing guard).

7) Three tickets resolved AGAINST their own hypothesis and the spec deliberately keeps them visible: TabFM rejected (16), opportunity cases shown structurally unreachable (19), the power-layer critique accepted rather than answered (15). spec.md: 'A plan with no negative findings has not been tested.'

8) Load-bearing self-imposed guards a drift review should test the build against: 'each resolved ticket's full acceptance criteria stay the yardstick', 'every capability carries a depth grade (stub/partial/full)' travelling at runtime, 'code is disposable — the decisions endure', the published does-not-do register, and 'only as-consumed scores'.

9) The Flux hypothesis is the single explicitly unfalsified assumption carried into the build — held as 'integral enabler unless proven otherwise', with the test recorded in ticket 22 and repeated in both map and spec. If the build shipped Flux without running that test, that is drift the decision record predicted.

10) One internal tension inside the decisions themselves: ticket 09/10/15 make the £ perspectival and contestability primary, while ticket 15's own adversarial pass concludes the perspectival £ is 'the tell' that converts a power asymmetry into a plurality of viewpoints — accepted rather than resolved. The group knowingly ships that contradiction.

decisions.title: Does the rule-set delta need `extends` to be readable? (intra-policy DRY)
decisions.status: Verdict: a rendered-artefact diff is ENOUGH. Inheritance leaves this map.
decisions.gist: Answers the narrow question of whether a policy version must extend its own predecessor. The release gate never consumes the textual delta — it consumes facts, a CEL expression list, and corpus verdict movement, so a rendered-artefact diff suffices; source-level inheritance would be a real DRY win but is out of scope for the gate.

decisions.title: Cross-party policy composition — can a party's effective policy set be inherited from other parties?
decisions.status: Verdict: composition is a real and missing layer. It changes what "the candidate version" is, so the gate computes the bump after composition.
decisions.gist: Composition (nist controls -> platform implementations -> adopter, plus ico pricing and threat/CVE/EOL feeds as non-rule-contributing parents) is modeled as class-like inheritance with no override: a subclass that cannot meet a rule is caged and priced, never exempted. The write-up records an explicit self-correction: an earlier draft's claim that 'the diamond needs no override rule: divergence is priced, not merged' is withdrawn as fusing two different mechanisms — conflicts are refused, not priced.

decisions.title: Does C2P v2 correctly consume PolicyReports from a CEL ValidatingPolicy?
decisions.status: Verdict: YES, with a ~6-line collection-time shim. Verified 2026-07-14 on KiND + Kyverno 1.18.2 + C2P v2.0.0-rc.1.
decisions.gist: C2P result2oscal keys only on results[].policy (string-equal to Check_Id), which Kyverno populates identically for ClusterPolicy and ValidatingPolicy, so the mechanism works. The one real gap is that Kyverno >=1.18 puts the subject in .scope with results[].resources null, causing 0 subjects captured (false negative) unless a jq shim copies .scope into results[].resources.

decisions.title: Renovate git-refs customManager vs the nested {version, commit} array (PRD S10)
decisions.status: Verdict: YES. Verified 2026-07-14 against Renovate 42.99.0.
decisions.gist: One customManagers regex entry with a git-refs datasource correctly bumps both the flat spec.ref.{tag,commit} pin and the nested spec.defaultValues.policyVersions[].{version,commit} array shape, because the regex matches the two adjacent lines regardless of nesting depth. The PRD S6.2 customManager design is sound as specified; issue 11 (multi-entry arrays) can proceed on this pattern.

decisions.title: Can native Kubernetes CEL (ValidatingAdmissionPolicy) replace Kyverno for the floor?
decisions.status: Verdict: partial — native CEL cannot replace Kyverno for the floor as designed; it can only replace the gating half.
decisions.gist: Native VAP/VAPBinding (GA in K8s 1.30) faithfully substitutes the admission gate, Deny/Audit axis, multi-version coexistence, and Crossplane-CR targeting, but has three architectural gaps with no version that closes them: no PolicyReports, no background scan, and Audit only writes to the API-server audit log on failure. Recommended posture: Kyverno stays the floor engine; native VAP is a credible north-star/engine-agnostic option and a belt-and-braces second gate, not a replacement.

notes: ["spikes/ contains a .DS_Store and, inside spikes/c2p-real-job/.work/, a full nested git clone of the upstream `c2p` project (its own .git, .github, dependabot config, etc.) — this is build/scratch output of the spike (gitignored per its README's Files section: '.work/ (gitignored) built C2P, venv, schema cache, generated OSCAL'), not authored documentation, and was excluded from the file inventory read for this task.","cs-06-inheritance-vs-diff/README.md and cs-06b-cross-party-composition/README.md form an explicit two-part narrative: cs-06 answers a narrower question than the original ticket intended and hands off to cs-06b, which states outright 'This replaces the question cs-06 originally wrote down.' A reviewer comparing 'decided' vs 'built' should read the two together, not independently — cs-06's verdict about inheritance not being needed applies only to intra-policy DRY, not to cross-party composition, which cs-06b affirms as real and missing.","cs-06b/README.md is unusually self-annotated with strikethrough corrections (~~old claim~~ -> closed by ticket N) documenting its own claims changing over time as later tickets closed gaps it originally listed as open; the current file state already reflects tickets 06, 12, 17, 18 as closing four of its five original 'what this prototype does not do' items, leaving only 'the rule-conflict refusal is untested across parties' still open.","Two spikes (c2p-real-job and c2p-validatingpolicy-oscal) are explicitly sibling/successor: c2p-real-job's README states its sibling was 'the mechanism spike (toy policies, proved C2P consumes CEL ValidatingPolicy reports at all — risk-retired)' and that c2p-real-job adds independent schema validation the mechanism spike skipped — read them as a pair, not as duplicate coverage.","The explorations/ directory contains exactly one file and is explicitly marked in its own text as 'Standalone exploration — not woven into the existing docs' — unlike the spikes/, which are tied to specific tracker tickets (ADR/PRD/issue numbers), this document has no ticket ID of its own and is a freestanding architecture-options analysis.","No decision ticket or ADR file itself lives inside spikes/ or explorations/ — all decision/ADR sourcing here is the spikes'/exploration's own verdict statements (self-contained spike verdicts) plus references out to ADRs and issue trackers that live elsewhere in the repo (not read as part of this group's scope).","No ticket in this group records a bare 'agree'/'yes'/single-letter owner response; all statuses found are the spike author's own verdict/finding write-ups, so depends_on_bare_agree is empty for every decision listed."]

thesis_or_destination: "This batch (build tickets 61-91) is the closing phase of the twin project's build: it populates the honesty-of-scope machinery (affected-parties register, misuse catalogues, does-not-do register, depth grades that travel automatically with every artefact), builds and runs the three-subject demo (Royal Mail for falsifiability, Netflix for the whole engine and cross-domain £ comparison, Intel for a live unresolved forecast, plus Kodak/Maersk as a lighter portfolio tier), instruments and (attempts to) measure real-world Flux drift, and then works ticket-by-ticket down every remaining capability's unchecked acceptance criteria until, at build ticket 91, 'demo-slice' closes and the published capability aggregate reaches 73 of 73 across all thirteen shipped capabilities. Ticket 77 states the destination most explicitly: 'anticipation and provable falsifiability first, then proportionate versioned governance, concluding in the one-currency comparison — the most seductive and least self-evident claim, earned rather than opened with. Lead with the £ and the sharpest person in the room rightly asks where the number came from. The order is the argument: earn credibility, then spend it.' Running underneath the demo work is a second, harder thread — the Flux falsification test (tickets 64/65/70/78) — whose destination is explicitly to 'run the test rather than assume the answer' and which, honestly, never reaches a resolved verdict inside this batch: the probe was never scheduled, the coverage floor became permanently unreachable, and the owner recorded that outcome rather than fixing it."
notes: ["Numbering note: the requested range was 'files numbered 61 to 92', but no build ticket 92 exists in the directory — the highest numbered file is 91-demo-slice-the-rendered-artefact.md, which is explicitly the batch's own final ticket (blocked by 90, closes the last capability to full). This inventory covers 61 through 91 in full; there is nothing at 92 to omit.", "The Flux/drift thread (tickets 64, 65, 70's finding 1, 78) is the single largest unresolved honesty thread in this batch: instrumentation was built and even adversarially/confirmatorily audited multiple times, yet the crontab was never installed and the owner was directly asked and directly declined to fix it (recorded at ticket 70's audit). Every ticket from 70 onward through 91 carries the identical two pre-existing 'known, red' invariant failures (drift_window_is_actually_being_sampled, flux_coverage_floor_is_still_reachable) in its own evidence section, explicitly named as unrelated and pre-existing rather than fixed — this is a consistent, self-reported, un-remediated gap running through the entire second half of the batch.", "A running pattern across nearly every ticket from 79 onward: closing a capability to 'full' moves twin/capabilities/*.yaml's digest, which moves every artefact's embedded capabilities_digest pin, which breaks the committed golden-digest byte fixtures — each ticket re-blesses them via a gated 'twin verify --bless-goldens --authorise' command citing the decision ticket. This is disclosed consistently and does not appear to be corner-cutting, but a reviewer should note it is the same mechanical consequence recurring roughly ten times (79, 81, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 87, 88, 89, 90, 91) — worth checking whether any one of those re-blessings was rubber-stamped rather than genuinely re-verified.", "Ticket 90 surfaces a real, self-reported inconsistency the project chose NOT to fix: ethics-gate was reclassified from 'skill' to 'code' after genuine investigation, but the 'six real skills' framing remains unchanged in twin/skills.py's module docstring, skill-thresholds.yaml, five other skill modules' own 'Nth of six' docstrings, a test file's _EXPECTED_SKILLS, and .scratch/twin/map.md — described by the ticket itself as a deliberate, named, unclosed gap rather than scope creep. A drift reviewer comparing 'what decision ticket 20 says' against 'what the codebase's prose still says' will find a live contradiction.", "Several tickets (64, 65, 66) carry unusual 'not done' status lines that read almost as red-team self-corrections: 'instrumented, NOT MEASURING — corrected 2026-08-10', 'pre-registered, VERDICT PENDING', 'refusal built, PR CHANNEL NOT WIRED'. These are unusually candid for build-ticket status lines and should be weighed as genuine signal, not noise — the project's own convention (named explicitly at ticket 70) is that a non-done status names precisely what is missing rather than hiding it.", "Ticket 90's investigated tension and ticket 82's reversed tick (on twin-inside-twin AC5) are two concrete examples in this batch of self-correction working as designed — worth citing positively if the drift review is looking for evidence the honesty machinery actually functions, not just that gaps exist.", "Two dated real-world tech-evolution signals recur across multiple tickets as load-bearing evidence for build sequencing/scope decisions: AWS Dogwood (2026-08-06, evaluated and explicitly rejected for the enactment arm at tickets 65/66/69) and the Cowgill & Zitzewitz corporate-prediction-market study (cited at ticket 63 for the twin's own adoption-risk scenario). Both are treated as 'signals about the world', not merely product literature."]

thesis_or_destination: "Most build tickets under .scratch/twin/ are closed; 64 is instrumented and measuring, not closed. One dated signal binds to a component; one scenario execution emits forecasts — plural; one recorded outcome scores them under proper scoring rules; any artefact recomputes from its own pins. Scoring is in the first slice rather than retrofitted, because without it we cannot tell whether any later capability helped, and because scoring dictates what every other component must record." The tool builds a governed 'digital twin' model repository — world layer + org overlays, typed graph, causal propagation, £ pricing gated by evidence grade, forecast scoring under proper scoring rules, and a propose-only enactment posture — with every artefact pinned, signed, and reproducible from its own pins.

decisions.title: Settle what "organisation" means before the split hard-codes the ambiguity
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: No collective noun for the six — name the kind ('the platform, two regulators and three institutions'); all six are independent GitHub organisations. Roles compose (publisher / risk-bearer / adopter) and platform is publisher+risk-bearer, carrying its own £10k band. `org` stays overloaded but documented (renaming churns artefact provenance). Terms written into CONTEXT.md; the demo's entitled sentence is settled and only sayable once the split lands.
decisions.depends_on_bare_agree: No bare agree recorded; the answer records specific owner calls ('The owner's call, and the estate already proves it' on role composition) but not a bare yes/letter.

decisions.title: Decide the split mechanics and how cross-org verification works
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 03
decisions.gist: Platform ships the verify harness as a pinned dependency and the hub runs the cross-cutting beats; `verify/` and `talk/` become their own repos in the hub org; tags are dual-signed (gitsign + OpenPGP) because Flux's spec.verify only speaks OpenPGP — a time-boxed bridge that must link the upstream Flux issue. Only 4 scripts carry a single-tree assumption. Regulator pins stay direct and estate/README.md:19's nist/ico → platform → institutions chain is false and must be corrected. Keys per-org as GitHub Actions org secrets, backed to 1Password.
decisions.depends_on_bare_agree: No bare agree; the owner input recorded is substantive (meta/curated packages, multiple regulators, customer SLAs) and was spun out to ticket 17.

decisions.title: Should the estate gain a prediction-market signal feed?
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 05
decisions.gist: Benchmark only — and in practice no estate work. Market price moves may grade forecasts, never price a control. The twin's own research measured overlap at ~1 of 10 scenario families and 0% of the org overlay. Mechanism stays in twin/market_signals.py under `price_levels_never_probabilities`; no sixth feed, no shared library, no extraction.

decisions.title: The forward layer can only ever raise the bill (monotone pessimism)
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: Yes — a commoditising defence may lower cost, through cost-of-controls (not LEF), gated on corroborated enactment. The estate has no corroboration mechanism today (`wargamer.py:138`'s `deployed_move` is a declared field defaulting to whatever the engine would pick), so the gate must be built rather than borrowed from the twin's pricing._credit()/NOT_ENACTED shape.

decisions.title: An institution answers to many masters, and the estate models one
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: Overlap and duplication are permanent and expected, not to be normalised away; obligations scope per-workload, not per-institution; one breach can draw several consequences and the £ takes the worst case; genuine deadlock gets a deferred reconciler which must resolve between obligations, never waive one (exemptions are a banned concept). Curated bundles are a convenience, never the only path. ico's parallel feed stack is evidence the shared kind is already wanted.
decisions.depends_on_bare_agree: The owner's answers are recorded as short direct quotes ('there will always be duplications and overlap.', 'they may not all apply to all workloads.', 'the org may be subject to multiple fines or other consequences for a single breach, so you may need to consider the worst case scenario.', 'we may later need to consider an overrides or reconciler stage...') — substantive, not bare agrees. The ticket explicitly records that 'The owner's answer overrode the recommendation on conflict handling, and the correction is recorded rather than smoothed over.'

thesis_or_destination: map.md Destination: "**A policy release states its bump and is refused if the evidence disagrees.** The release gate evaluates the candidate version and its predecessor against a corpus, observes how verdicts move on currently-compliant workloads, derives **major / minor / patch** from `CONTEXT.md`'s existing definition, and fails the release when the declared bump contradicts what was measured." Plus: "The same rule binds the **platform's own version**, not just the policy body — a platform bump changes the version array, which changes which policies run, which changes verdicts. The distribution layer does not get to exempt itself from the rule it distributes." Map title: "the version number computes itself". spec.md Solution: "A release states its bump. The gate measures the bump. The gate refuses the release when the two disagree in the unsafe direction." Standing preferences: "The engine must reproduce a human's correct answer before it is trusted to give its own." and "Honesty over green — a gate that passes because the corpus missed the case is this estate's favourite bug, and it has three already. Coverage must be stated, not implied."

decisions.title: What counts as a "verdict", given Audit is not a pass
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: Compliant means admitted; an Audit rule that fires reports and does not fail. There is no separate refused verdict class — refusal is the bottom rung of the cage ladder, a pure function of (residual, band). Every workload is always caged and the cage SPEC is what changes, so the engine compares cage specs not verdict enums. The bump is institution-relative: compute against the strictest band and tag that, publishing the per-institution matrix. Unversioned/COTS workloads are a permanent population, spun out as its own effort.
decisions.depends_on_bare_agree: No bare agree; owner answers are quoted at length ("the pod stopping is just the implementation of the incoming policy because it does not fit in an available cage...", "you're always caged even if it's a permissive one. It's the spec of the cage that can change.", "there'll always be COTS products that we must facilitate and support").

decisions.title: What represents "currently-compliant workloads"? (the corpus)
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 01
decisions.gist: The corpus is a GENERATED population of plain pods owned by `platform`, enumerated per CEL expression (satisfied/violated/absent) plus a version-pin axis and a tier-label axis, combined pairwise, generated from both subjects and unioned. A second WITNESS set of real workloads proves the generator; a witness shape missing from the spine fails the build and the repair is always the generator. The corpus is not signed (regenerated and diffed in CI); the evidence output is signed. Movement traced to an unversioned policy fails the gate and names the file.
decisions.depends_on_bare_agree: Not a bare agree; recorded as seven rounds of grilling driven by four environment facts, two of which overturned decisions taken earlier in the same session.

decisions.title: How is incomplete coverage stated rather than implied?
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 03
decisions.gist: No coverage percentage at all — a percentage invites a threshold and a threshold invites tuning the corpus. The gate publishes counts plus a not-looked-at list, each entry carrying a stable id (hash of the normalised expression text scoped by identity family and version-stripped policy name). Three binary gates replace the threshold: unreached predicate, missing witness shape, movement on an unversioned policy. Limits are derived by the check that would remove them and print as closed rather than vanishing. Evidence is always emitted and signed, including on refusal. Corrects cs-03's "per CEL expression" to predicate expressions only.
decisions.depends_on_bare_agree: No owner answer recorded verbatim; "Resolved by grilling, 2026-08-22, over three rounds" driven by two environment facts.

decisions.title: Where the gate runs, and what happens when it disagrees with the human
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 02, 03
decisions.gist: Two gates asking two different questions and no override at all. The publisher gate runs in `cut-release.yml`, reads the declared bump from the `version` input, runs before `git tag`, refuses a weaker declared bump, permits a stronger one, never rewrites. The adopter gate runs in each institution's `shift-left.yml` and computes that institution's own composed bump. Comparison is against every supported lower version in the window as it stood before this release. Version legality follows semver 2.0.0 (reset on bump enforced, gaps legal). Evidence signed `cosign sign-blob` keyless, removing the `feeds/sign.sh` ed25519 shape. Two live bugs found.
decisions.depends_on_bare_agree: No bare agree. Two of the author's own recommendations are recorded as corrected — one by the owner on release-lifecycle grounds ("The owner rejected 'strictly greater than every existing tag'") and one by the semver specification itself.

decisions.title: Does the rule-set delta need inheritance to be readable?
decisions.status: Type: prototype / Status: resolved / Blocked by: 01
decisions.gist: For a policy version extending its own predecessor: no, a rendered-artefact diff is enough, because the gate never classifies from the delta. Four findings the gate must carry: parse the YAML never text-diff; the identity label is a family name not a unique key so pair on (identity, name-with-version-stripped) and fail on an unversioned member; compare rules as a set; treat a version-literal difference as unproven. A Correction section records the ticket body wrote down the wrong (narrow) question, moves the real cross-party question to the `policy-composition` map, and withdraws "inheritance leaves this map".
decisions.depends_on_bare_agree: No owner answer recorded; conclusions are prototype-derived (`spikes/cs-06-inheritance-vs-diff/`, branch `cs-06-cross-party-composition`, `36000ef`).

thesis_or_destination: map.md Destination: "**A party's effective policy set is composed from other parties' signed, versioned artefacts, and the composition is refused when it does not hold together.** Policy as a dependency you *extend and mash up*, not only pin. A regulator publishes **controls**; a publisher ships **implementations**; an adopter inherits both and adds its own. Pricing and threat parents contribute no rules but move the £." spec.md title: "a party's policy is composed from its parents, and refused when it does not hold"; spec.md scope: "**the composition step on the adopter side**, from the adopter's pinned parents to a signed composed artefact, plus the inputs the other parties must publish for it to run." map.md label `wayfinder:map`, charted 2026-08-21, "split out of `computed-semver` ... after its ticket 09 grew a compliance architecture that had nothing to do with computing a bump."

decisions.title: Policy inherits across parties, not just across versions (Does composition hold up?)
decisions.status: Type: prototype / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: Yes, cross-party composition is a real missing layer; prototype `spikes/cs-06b-cross-party-composition/` composes the estate and renders back down to committed per-version files. Caging settles only a child that cannot meet a parent; two parents whose rules disagree is refused, not merged, and is untested across parties (one implementations publisher). Pricing/threat parents are wired and the price moves, but no real feed bump changes a decision. Four gaps found, only one needed composition to find.

decisions.title: What gets signed
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: The adopter self-signs the composed artefact with the same gitsign-signed git tag it already uses; no second signing mechanism. A parent's "digest" is its resolved commit SHA (the one Renovate already pins), recorded once at the top of the composed artefact. Verification stays CI/merge-time only. Recorded as ADR-0012 plus a new CONTEXT.md **Composed artefact** term.

decisions.title: Who declares the baseline, and against which catalogue ids
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: The regulator publishes named baselines as OSCAL profiles; the adopter selects one by name (this estate selects MODERATE); both key on the bare catalogue id (`ac-6`, never `AC-6`, never `nist-800-53:AC-6`), resolved exact-string with no case-folding and no prefix-stripping, walking nested controls. Adopter may add a control, never remove. 285 holes on day one; a composition refuses on a NEW hole only, against the last signed composed artefact. Recorded as ADR-0013 plus **Baseline** and **Control id** terms.

decisions.title: Whether an unlabelled pod is denied
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: The committed orphan guard is correct and `CONTEXT.md` was wrong about the guard but right that a hole exists. Absence of the claim label is never the deny trigger (cluster-scoped guard would brick the cluster; de-posture depends on the skip). A de-postured pod is caged, keeps running, priced. A sibling `ValidatingPolicy` scoped by `policy-as-versioned.dev/governed: "true"` and matching `CREATE` only closes the silence. Recorded as ADR-0014 plus **Governed namespace** and **De-postured** terms.

decisions.title: The proposer
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: A proposer already exists (`platform/wargamer/`), the adopter runs it in its own repo on its own `GITHUB_TOKEN` through its pinned `platform` dependency, and it now opens the PR editing `posture.acme.io/tier` on a workload manifest. A cage-tier drift is a third drift row. A merged Renovate pin bump or `workflow_dispatch` starts a run; never a clock. Sixth gap named: `select_tier` returns `deny`, the label cannot carry it, `cage-tier` coerces to `baseline`, so a merged Deny inverts. Recorded as ADR-0015 plus a **Proposer** term.

decisions.title: Composing the five unversioned live policies
decisions.status: Type: prototype / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: Composition holds across the whole live set and every kind renders back down faithfully; four of the five formerly-unversioned policies are now versioned by `cs-12`'s renderer, the fifth (orphan guard) cannot be versioned and carries a second numbering axis under the `platform-machinery` identity. Three findings: an action is a ValidatingPolicy concept so a subclass cannot tighten a mutate; the identity label is a family not a key; mutation ordering is inherited, not declared, and is ruled `platform` machinery. Recorded as ADR-0016.

decisions.title: What fills a control the adopter adds itself
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: A control is filled by a signed OSCAL control claim from whoever ships the implementation — an inherited publisher, the adopter's own member, or a third pinned publisher. An adopter-added hole is an ordinary new hole with no on-purpose flag. The adopter's claim lives in its own component-definition; an adopter may never claim against another party's policy and may never remove a control it added. Recorded as ADR-0017 plus a **Control claim** term.

decisions.title: Does a composed artefact declare its governed namespaces
decisions.status: Type: grilling / Status: resolved / Blocked by: none
decisions.gist: No. The `governed: "true"` label on the adopter's own Namespace manifest is the declaration; the composed artefact records the set as advisory metadata only. A composition refuses a NEW ungoverned adopter namespace (institution label, no governed label) and records a pre-existing one. The governed set narrows the `CREATE` claim rule and nothing else. Only the adopter adds a namespace, by hand. Recorded as ADR-0018.
decisions.depends_on_bare_agree: Close to it: the Answer records only "Resolved 2026-08-25 by grilling. All five recommendations accepted." — a bare blanket acceptance of all five recommendations, with no per-item owner reasoning recorded.
